MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html:3638:<p>The presheaf \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) is generally not an étale (or even Zariski) sheaf. The standard obstruction (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302): for a \(k\)-scheme \(T\) carrying a non-trivial line bundle whose pullback to \(C \times _k T\) becomes non-trivial after an open cover, the Zariski separated-presheaf condition fails. Therefore, to obtain a representable functor in the sense of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html">25</a>, one must replace \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) by its <em>associated étale sheaf</em>. Kleiman §2 names this sheaf \(\operatorname{Pic}_{(X/S)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\) and singles it out as the functor that Kleiman’s main existence theorem in §4 represents. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html:3699:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §2, Def. df:Pfs (the étale-sheaf notation \(\operatorname{Pic}_{(X/S)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\)) and the associated-sheaf paragraph immediately following df:Pfs.</i> Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve. The <em>étale-sheafified relative Picard functor</em> is the sheafification of the presheaf \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html#thm:rel_pic_sharp_presheaf">623</a>) in the global étale topology on \((\operatorname{Sch}/k)\): </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html:3703:<p> Equivalently, \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\) is the unique (up to canonical isomorphism) sheaf of abelian groups on the étale site of \(\operatorname{Sch}/k\) equipped with a presheaf morphism \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k} \to \operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\) which is universal among presheaf morphisms from \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) to étale sheaves of abelian groups. In Kleiman’s notation this is \(\operatorname{Pic}_{(X/S)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\) with \(X = C\) and \(S = \operatorname{Spec}k\). When \(k\) is algebraically closed and \(T = \operatorname{Spec}k'\) for an algebraically closed field extension \(k'/k\), the natural map \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}(T) \to \operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(T)\) is a bijection (Kleiman Exercise ex:Alr, L1357–L1361). </p>

There exists a canonical morphism of presheaves of abelian groups </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html:3874:  <p>In any Grothendieck topology, every presheaf has a canonical associated sheaf, and the canonical morphism from a presheaf to its associated sheaf is universal among morphisms from the presheaf into sheaves (Stacks tag 00WI; Kleiman §2, paragraph following df:Pfs). The étale site of \((\operatorname{Sch}/k)\) is a Grothendieck topology, so this applies in particular to \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) and yields the canonical set-valued sheafification \((\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k})^{\sim _\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\) together with the universal arrow out of \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\). The forgetful functor \(\mathrm{AddCommGroup}\to \mathbf{Set}\) preserves and reflects the filtered colimits and finite limits used by the plus-construction, so performing the same plus-construction inside \(\mathrm{AddCommGroup}\) yields a sheaf of abelian groups whose underlying set-valued sheaf coincides with the set-valued sheafification; the abelian-group structure on the sheafification is transported back through this identification. The resulting morphism \(\eta \) is then by construction the universal arrow in the abelian-group-valued sheafification, which is the universal property in the form stated. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html:3890:  <li><p><span class="ttfamily">AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicSharp.etSheaf</span> (<a href="chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html#def:rel_pic_etale_sheafification">627</a>) is the étale sheafification of <span class="ttfamily">PicSharp</span>. The Lean form is <span class="ttfamily">CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf</span> applied to the big étale topology on <span class="ttfamily">Scheme</span> with target category <span class="ttfamily">AddCommGrpCat</span>. <b class="bfseries">Lean API note.</b> The big étale Grothendieck topology on the category of schemes is <span class="ttfamily">AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology</span>, of type <span class="ttfamily">CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme</span> (module <span class="ttfamily">Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Etale</span>; an <span class="ttfamily">abbrev</span> for the topology generated by the big étale pretopology <span class="ttfamily">Scheme.etalePretopology</span>). The sheafification entry point with abelian-group target is <span class="ttfamily">CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology AddCommGrpCat</span>, of type <span class="ttfamily">Functor (Schemeᵒᵖ \(\Rightarrow \) AddCommGrpCat) (Sheaf etaleTopology AddCommGrpCat)</span> (module <span class="ttfamily">Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.Sheafification</span>); it is available under a <span class="ttfamily">CategoryTheory.HasWeakSheafify</span> instance for the pair <span class="ttfamily">(etaleTopology, AddCommGrpCat)</span>. The slice \((\operatorname{Sch}/k)\) on the Lean side is captured by working over the global <span class="ttfamily">Scheme</span> category and restricting along <span class="ttfamily">Over (Spec k)</span> via Mathlib’s <span class="ttfamily">CategoryTheory.Sites.Over</span> / <span class="ttfamily">GrothendieckTopology</span> pullback construction (the relative Picard functor’s natural domain is the slice; Kleiman’s notation \((\operatorname{Sch}/S)^{op}\) corresponds to <span class="ttfamily">(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ</span>). If the <span class="ttfamily">HasWeakSheafify</span> instance for the pair <span class="ttfamily">(etaleTopology, AddCommGrpCat)</span> is missing at the pinned Mathlib commit, the project-side fallback combines the concrete set-valued sheafification <span class="ttfamily">CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.sheafify</span> (module <span class="ttfamily">Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.ConcreteSheafification</span>) with the colimit-preservation of the forgetful functor \(\texttt{AddCommGrpCat} \to \mathbf{Set}\) and the <span class="ttfamily">plusPlusSheaf</span> plus-construction on the underlying set-valued presheaf, transported back through the <span class="ttfamily">ConcreteCategory</span> instance on <span class="ttfamily">AddCommGrpCat</span>. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html:3895:<p>The relationship with <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html">25</a> is captured by the slogan: the FGA Picard scheme of A.2.c represents \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\) (Kleiman §4, the main existence theorem: “…represents \(\operatorname{Pic}_{(X/S)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\)”), <em>not</em> \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) directly. MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:2977:          <li><a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen">Lemma 1247</a></li>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:3020:  <p> Write \(\beta := p^\sharp _{U_0, W_j}(g) \in B_j := \Gamma (X, W_j)\), so that \(D(\beta ) = W_j \cap p^{-1}(D(g))\). By the quasi-compact–quasi-separated section-localization theorem (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen">1247</a>, applied to the affine \(W_j\)), the restriction \(\Gamma (\mathcal F, W_j) \to \Gamma (\mathcal F, D(\beta ))\) is the localization of \(B_j\)-modules at the powers of \(\beta \); since \(\beta ^k\) acts on these modules as \(g^k\) acts through \(p^\sharp \), it is also the localization of \(A\)-modules at the powers of \(g\). Hence \(\Gamma (\mathcal F, D(\beta )) \cong \Gamma (\mathcal F, W_j)_g\) is free, in particular flat, over \(A_g\), and therefore flat over \(A\) (flatness over \(A\) and over the localization \(A_g\) agree for \(A_g\)-modules). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:3021:<p>Since \(D(c) \subseteq D(\beta )\), the further restriction \(\Gamma (\mathcal F, D(\beta )) \to \Gamma (\mathcal F, D(c))\) is again a section localization (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen">1247</a> on the affine \(D(\beta )\), at the restricted element \(c|_{D(\beta )}\), whose basic open is \(D(c)\)) — a localization of \(\Gamma (X, D(\beta ))\)-modules. Mixed-base stability (<a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:flat_localizedModule_algebra">923</a>, with base \(A\) and fibre algebra \(\Gamma (X, D(\beta ))\)) shows \(\Gamma (\mathcal F, D(c|_{D(\beta )}))\) is flat over \(A\); the induced-structure compatibilities are <a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:appLE_res_apply">924</a>, and <a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:flat_sections_congr">926</a> transports the conclusion along \(D(c|_{D(\beta )}) = D(c)\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:3063:          <li><a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen">Lemma 1247</a></li>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:3109:<p>The basic opens \(D(b)\) obtained this way cover \(W\), so the chosen elements \(b\) generate the unit ideal of \(\Gamma (X, W)\). Since each restriction \(\Gamma (\mathcal F, W) \to \Gamma (\mathcal F, D(b))\) is a localization of \(\Gamma (X, W)\)-modules at the powers of \(b\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen">1247</a>), flatness of \(\Gamma (\mathcal F, W)\) over \(\Gamma (S, U)\) may be checked on the pieces \(\Gamma (\mathcal F, D(b))\) (flatness over the base is local with respect to a spanning family of the fibre algebra). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:3152:          <li><a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:affine_finite_sections_nhds">Lemma 1258</a></li>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:3195:  <p> Choose a non-empty affine open \(U_0 \subseteq S\); its section ring \(A := \Gamma (S, U_0)\) is a noetherian domain because \(S\) is integral and locally noetherian. The preimage \(p^{-1}(U_0)\) is quasi-compact (\(p\) is quasi-compact and \(U_0\) is), and every point of it has an affine open neighbourhood inside \(p^{-1}(U_0)\) on which the sections of \(\mathcal{F}\) are a finite module over the sections of \(\mathcal{O}_X\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:affine_finite_sections_nhds">1258</a>); extract a finite subcover by affine charts \(W^{(1)}, \dots , W^{(r)}\). Each \(B_i := \Gamma (X, W^{(i)})\) is of finite type over \(A\) (as \(p\) is locally of finite type and both opens are affine) and each \(M_i := \Gamma (\mathcal{F}, W^{(i)})\) is a finite \(B_i\)-module, so algebraic generic freeness (<a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#thm:generic_flatness_algebraic">922</a>) produces \(f_i \in A \setminus \{ 0\} \) with \((M_i)_{f_i}\) free over \(A_{f_i}\). Set \(f := f_1 \cdots f_r \ne 0\); freeness localizes from each \(f_i\) to \(f\), so every \((M_i)_f\) is free over \(A_f\). The witness open is \(V := D(f) \subseteq U_0\), non-empty because \(S\) is reduced and \(f \ne 0\). The required flatness on every affine pair \(U \subseteq V\), \(W \subseteq p^{-1}(U)\) is exactly the two-layer basic-open reduction, <a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:flat_section_pair">928</a>. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:3418:          <li><a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#thm:flat_base_change_cohomology">Theorem 1222</a></li>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:3629:          <li><a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:pullback_app_isoTensor_sigma">Definition 1243</a></li>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:3676:  <p>Restricting the cartesian square over the affine cospan \(U_X \to U_S \leftarrow U_T\) exhibits \(U_Y\) as the fibre product \(U_X \times _{U_S} U_T\) of affine schemes, which is affine. Applying global sections to this pullback and using the anti-equivalence between affine schemes and commutative rings yields the pushout of section rings. Since \(U_Y \subseteq g^{-1}(U_X)\) with \(U_X\), \(U_Y\) affine and \(\mathcal{F}\) quasi-coherent, the base-change section formula (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:pullback_app_isoTensor_sigma">1243</a>, Stacks 01HQ/01I8) identifies \(\Gamma (g^* \mathcal{F}, U_Y) \cong \Gamma (Y, U_Y) \otimes _{\Gamma (X, U_X)} \Gamma (\mathcal{F}, U_X)\) as \(\Gamma (Y, U_Y)\)-modules, i.e. exhibits \(\Gamma (g^*\mathcal{F}, U_Y)\) as a base change of \(\Gamma (\mathcal{F}, U_X)\) along \(\Gamma (X, U_X) \to \Gamma (Y, U_Y)\). Flatness over \(\Gamma (T, U_T)\) is now <a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:flat_pushout_base_change">935</a> applied to the section-ring pushout square; finiteness is preserved because a base change of a finite module is finite. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:3757:  <p>This is the two-layer basic-open reduction of <a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:flat_section_pair">928</a>, with the freeness input replaced by chart flatness. Fix an affine pair \((U, W)\). For each \(x \in W\) choose a chart \(W_j \ni x\); since \(q(x) \in U \cap U_j\) and both are affine, there is a basic open \(D(a) = D(a')\) of \(T\) common to \(U\) and \(U_j\) containing \(q(x)\), and then a basic open \(D(b) = D(c) \ni x\) common to \(W\) and \(W_j\) with \(D(b) \subseteq q^{-1}(D(a))\). The elements \(b\) generate the unit ideal of \(\Gamma (Y, W)\), and each restriction \(\Gamma (\mathcal G, W) \to \Gamma (\mathcal G, D(b))\) is a localization at the powers of \(b\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen">1247</a>), so flatness of \(\Gamma (\mathcal G, W)\) over \(\Gamma (T, U)\) may be checked on the pieces \(\Gamma (\mathcal G, D(b))\). On a piece: flatness of \(\Gamma (\mathcal G, W_j)\) over \(\Gamma (T, U_j)\) passes to the fibre-side localization \(\Gamma (\mathcal G, D(c))\) (mixed-base stability of flatness under localization of the module at a submonoid of the fibre algebra), and then the base ring is exchanged twice along \(\Gamma (T, U_j) \to \Gamma (T, D(a')) = \Gamma (T, D(a))\) and \(\Gamma (T, U) \to \Gamma (T, D(a))\) (for a module over a localized ring, flatness over the ring and over its localization agree; the compatibility of the induced module structures is <a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:appLE_base_res_apply">925</a>). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:7148:          <li><a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:pullback_app_isoTensor_sigma">Definition 1243</a></li>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:7193:  <p> For the affine pair \((V, W)\) the sections of the pullback module satisfy the base-change formula \(\Gamma (g^*\mathcal G, W) \cong \Gamma (Y, W) \otimes _{\Gamma (X, V)} \Gamma (\mathcal G, V)\) as \(\Gamma (Y, W)\)-modules (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:pullback_app_isoTensor_sigma">1243</a>). Base change of \(P\) along \(g^\sharp \) (<a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#def:matrix_presentation_base_change">946</a>) is a matrix presentation of the right-hand side — the pulled-back sequence stays exact by right-exactness of the tensor product — with relation matrix \(g^\sharp (\psi )\), and transporting it along the base-change isomorphism changes neither the generator count nor the relation matrix. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:7395:          <li><a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:pullback_app_isoTensor_sigma">Definition 1243</a></li>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:7440:  <p> Cover \(T'\) by affine opens \(W\), each contained in the preimage of some affine open \(V \subseteq T\). For such a pair the section module \(\Gamma (g^*\mathcal G, W) \cong \Gamma (T', W) \otimes _{\Gamma (T, V)} \Gamma (\mathcal G, V)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:pullback_app_isoTensor_sigma">1243</a>) is a base change of the flat module \(\Gamma (\mathcal G, V)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:flat_sections_of_sheaf_flat">983</a>), hence flat over \(\Gamma (T', W)\). The pullback \(g^*\mathcal G\) is quasi-coherent, so <a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:sheaf_flat_of_flat_charts">984</a> upgrades the cover of flat section modules to flatness over \(T'\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:7566:          <li><a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:pullback_app_isoTensor_sigma">Definition 1243</a></li>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:7615:  <p> Choose an affine open \(V \ni g(y)\) and an affine open \(W \ni y\) with \(W \subseteq g^{-1}(V)\). By the base-change formula for sections (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:pullback_app_isoTensor_sigma">1243</a>), \(\Gamma (g^*\mathcal G, W) \cong \Gamma (Y, W) \otimes _{\Gamma (X, V)} \Gamma (\mathcal G, V)\). The prime \(\mathfrak q \subseteq \Gamma (Y, W)\) of \(y\) contracts along the induced ring map to the prime \(\mathfrak p \subseteq \Gamma (X, V)\) of \(g(y)\). By <a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:fiber_rank_congr">958</a> and base-change invariance of the fiber rank (<a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#thm:fiber_rank_base_change">957</a>), the fiber rank of \(\Gamma (g^*\mathcal G, W)\) at \(\mathfrak q\) equals the fiber rank of \(\Gamma (\mathcal G, V)\) at \(\mathfrak p\). These are the chart fibre ranks of \(g^*\mathcal G\) at \(y\) on \(W\) and of \(\mathcal G\) at \(g(y)\) on \(V\), i.e. the two point ranks (<a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:point_rank_eq_chart_fiber_rank">968</a>). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:7953:          <li><a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:affine_finite_sections_nhds">Lemma 1258</a></li>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:8000:  <p> Choose an affine open \(V \ni s\) on which \(M := \Gamma (\mathcal{F}, V)\) is a finite module over \(R := \Gamma (S, V)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:affine_finite_sections_nhds">1258</a>). Since \(S\) is locally noetherian, \(R\) is a noetherian ring, so the finite module \(M\) is finitely presented. Let \(\mathfrak p\) be the prime of \(s\) in \(R\) and \(e\) the fiber rank of \(M\) at \(\mathfrak p\); by <a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:point_rank_eq_chart_fiber_rank">968</a>, \(e\) is the point rank of \(\mathcal{F}\) at \(s\). The Nakayama prolongation (<a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#thm:nakayama_prolongation">956</a>) supplies \(g \notin \mathfrak p\) such that every localization of \(M\) away from \(g\) admits a matrix presentation by \(e\) generators; by quasi-coherence \(\Gamma (\mathcal{F}, D(g))\) is such a localization, so the basic open \(D(g) \subseteq V\) is an \(e\)-presentation chart, and it contains \(s\) because \(g \notin \mathfrak p\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:8761:          <li><a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:affine_finite_sections_nhds">Lemma 1258</a></li>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:8814:  <p> Let \(t_0\) be a point of the locus. Choose an affine open \(V \ni \varphi (t_0)\) on which \(\Gamma (\mathcal{F}, V)\) is finite over the noetherian ring \(\Gamma (S, V)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:affine_finite_sections_nhds">1258</a>), hence finitely presented, and an affine open \(W \ni t_0\) with \(W \subseteq \varphi ^{-1}(V)\). Set \(M := \Gamma (\varphi ^*\mathcal{F}, W)\) and \(R := \Gamma (T, W)\). Then \(M\) is flat over \(R\) (<a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:flat_sections_of_sheaf_flat">983</a>) and finitely presented: a matrix presentation of \(\Gamma (\mathcal{F}, V)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:exists_matrix_presentation">981</a>) pulls back to a matrix presentation of \(M\) (<a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:presentation_pullback_sections">982</a>), and a module with a matrix presentation is finitely presented (<a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#lem:matrix_presentation_fp">943</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Cohomology_FlatBaseChange.html:1729:<p><em>Why the active route suffices.</em> Everything downstream of this chapter — the Čech tensorial base-change isomorphism (the cosimplicial residual \(e\) of the Čech chapter) and, through it, the Kleiman-style representability inputs — consumes <em>only</em> a base-change isomorphism (a \(\mathrm{Nonempty}\) / \(\cong \) datum) that commutes with the restriction maps, <em>not</em> the assertion that the canonical map \(\beta \) is that isomorphism. The fresh \(e\) supplies exactly such an isomorphism, and by construction it commutes with restriction (it is glued from restriction-compatible affine pieces). The canonical map \(\operatorname {pushforwardBaseChangeMap}\) is not a protected declaration, so re-plumbing the downstream consumers to receive \(e\) is permitted. Consequently the key constituent of this chapter is Lemma <a href="chap-Cohomology_FlatBaseChange.html#lem:affine_pushforward_pullback_baseChange">129</a> and the gluing chain (§<a href="chap-Cohomology_FlatBaseChange.html#sec:fbc_gluing">5.5</a>) built on it; the canonical-mate nodes are retained for faithfulness but are off the critical path. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:1711:<h1 id="chap:Picard_QuotScheme">20 The Quot scheme</h1>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:1715:<p>Throughout this chapter, let \(S\) be a noetherian scheme, \(\pi : X \to S\) a projective morphism, \(L\) a relatively very ample line bundle on \(X\) over \(S\), and \(E\) a coherent sheaf on \(X\). The Quot construction packages the \(T\)-flat coherent quotients \(E_T \twoheadrightarrow \mathcal{F}\) of the pull-back \(E_T\) to \(X_T = X \times _S T\), modulo the equivalence \(\langle \mathcal{F}, q\rangle = \langle \mathcal{F}', q'\rangle \) defined by \(\ker (q) = \ker (q')\). Fixing the Hilbert polynomial \(\Phi (\lambda ) = \chi (\mathcal{F}|_{X_t}(\lambda )) \in \mathbb {Q}[\lambda ]\) (constant on connected \(T\) by flatness) stratifies the Quot functor into pieces \(\operatorname {Quot}^{\Phi ,L}_{E/X/S}\), each of which Grothendieck proved is representable by a projective \(S\)-scheme. This chapter develops the foundations of that picture: the Hilbert polynomial (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:hilbert_polynomial">1006</a>), the Quot functor (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:quot_functor">1126</a>), and the Grassmannian scheme (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:grassmannian_scheme">1164</a>) with its representability (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#thm:grassmannian_representable">1171</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:1779:  <p>[Hilbert polynomial]    nitsure-hilbert-quot <i class="itshape">Source: [Nitsure], §1 (FGA Explained Ch. 5); cf. [Hartshorne], III.5.2.</i> Let \(X \to S\) be a finite-type morphism of noetherian schemes and let \(L\) be a line bundle on \(X\). For a coherent sheaf \(\mathcal{F}\) on \(X\) whose schematic support is proper over \(S\) and a point \(s \in S\), write \(X_s\) for the fibre over \(s\), \(\mathcal{F}_s = \mathcal{F}|_{X_s}\) and \(L_s = L|_{X_s}\). The <em>Hilbert polynomial of \(\mathcal{F}\) at \(s\) relative to \(L\)</em> is the unique polynomial \(\Phi _{\mathcal{F},s} \in \mathbb {Q}[\lambda ]\) that agrees, for all \(m \gg 0\), with the graded Hilbert function (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:fiber_hilbert_function">1011</a>) </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:1783:<p> of the section module \(\bigoplus _{m \ge 0} \Gamma (X_s, \mathcal{F}_s \otimes L_s^{\otimes m})\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:sectionGradedModule">1010</a>), viewed as a finitely generated graded module over the homogeneous section ring \(\bigoplus _{m \ge 0} \Gamma (X_s, L_s^{\otimes m})\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:sectionGradedRing">1009</a>). Uniqueness of \(\Phi _{\mathcal{F},s}\) is unconditional (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:hilbertPolynomial_unique">1026</a>: two polynomials agreeing at all sufficiently large integers coincide); existence, for \(X_s\) proper over \(\kappa (s)\), \(L_s\) ample and \(\mathcal{F}_s\) coherent, is the content of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#thm:hilbertPoly_of_sectionModule">1031</a>. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:1794:<p>This section gives the graded-Hilbert-function construction that underlies <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:hilbert_polynomial">1006</a>. It first records how a fibre \(X_s\) of a family \(\pi : X \to S\) carries the data the construction consumes: the restrictions \(\mathcal{F}_s\) and \(L_s\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:fiber_module_restriction">1007</a>) and the \(\kappa (s)\)-vector-space structure on their sections (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:fiber_sections_module">1008</a>). Working over the fibre \(X_s\) with its ample line bundle \(L_s\) and coherent sheaf \(\mathcal{F}_s\), it builds the section graded ring (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:sectionGradedRing">1009</a>) and module (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:sectionGradedModule">1010</a>) together with the graded Hilbert function (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:fiber_hilbert_function">1011</a>), records their finite generation (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:sectionGradedModule_fg">1012</a>), and extracts the Hilbert polynomial (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#thm:hilbertPoly_of_sectionModule">1031</a>): the graded Hilbert–Serre rationality of the Hilbert series (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:gradedHilbertSerre_rational">1016</a>) combines with Mathlib’s polynomial-extraction lemma (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:hilbertPoly_exists_mathlib">1013</a>) in <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:hilbertPoly_of_isRatHilb">1027</a>, and the extracted polynomial is unique by <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:hilbertPolynomial_unique">1026</a>. The route uses only \(H^0\) (global sections), so it is independent of higher coherent cohomology. </p>

Then the section graded ring \(R(X_s, L_s)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:sectionGradedRing">1009</a>) is a Noetherian graded ring, and the section graded module \(M(X_s, \mathcal{F}_s, L_s)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:sectionGradedModule">1010</a>) is a finitely generated graded \(R(X_s, L_s)\)-module. In particular each component \(\Gamma (X_s, \mathcal{F}_s \otimes L_s^{\otimes m})\) is a finite-dimensional \(\kappa (s)\)-vector space. (For an ample \(L_s\) the same conclusions follow by passing to a very ample Veronese power; the very ample form stated here is the one consumed by the Quot-scheme construction.) </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:2460:<p><em>Status.</em> This is the substantive half of the graded Hilbert–Serre theorem (rationality of the Hilbert series of a finitely generated graded module). It is not covered by Mathlib: <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:hilbertPoly_exists_mathlib">1013</a> supplies only the converse polynomial-extraction step from a rational series, not the production of the rational series from the module. The argument is realised by an <em>ambient subquotient induction</em> (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_isRatHilb">1089</a>): the whole induction ranges over pairs of homogeneous submodules \(N' \le N\) of the single fixed graded module \(M\), and the Hilbert function is the ambient difference \(n \mapsto \dim _\kappa (N \cap M_n) - \dim _\kappa (N' \cap M_n)\). The class of such pairs is closed under the kernel and cokernel of multiplication by a degree-one element (each presented again as an ambient subquotient pair), so the inductive step never forms a graded quotient ring \(R/(x)\), a graded quotient module \(M/xM\), or a regrading of a derived carrier. The genuine Mathlib gap is thereby <em>avoided</em> rather than filled; the residual obligation is the short ambient bookkeeping of the subquotient blocks (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientHilb">1046</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_ker_coker">1065</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_degreewise_diff">1067</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_finite_transfer">1080</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_isRatHilb">1089</a>), each of which manipulates only ambient families \(n \mapsto N_{\mathrm{aux}} \cap M_n\) of submodules of \(M\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:2474:<p><em>Set-up of the ambient data.</em> Regard \(M\) as the fixed ambient graded \(\kappa \)-module with internal decomposition \(n \mapsto \mathcal{M}_n := M_n\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:sectionGradedModule">1010</a>); the components are finite-dimensional. For each basis vector \(x_i \in R_1\) let \(t_i : M \to M\) be multiplication by \(x_i\), a \(\kappa \)-linear endomorphism that raises degree by one (it sends \(M_n\) into \(M_{n+1}\), <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isHomogeneousElem_graded_smul_mathlib">1036</a>). Since \(R\) is commutative the \(t_i\) pairwise commute, and they trivially preserve the pair of homogeneous submodules \((N, N') = (\top , \bot )\). Because \(R\) is generated by \(x_1, \dots , x_r\) and \(M\) is finitely generated over \(R\), \(M\) is finitely generated as a module over the polynomial ring \(\kappa [x_1, \dots , x_r]\) acting through the \(t_i\); this is the finiteness condition required below. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:3386:  <p>[Defining property of the Hilbert polynomial]    Let \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) be the graded Hilbert function of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:fiber_hilbert_function">1011</a>. If <em>some</em> polynomial in \(\mathbb {Q}[\lambda ]\) agrees with \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) at all sufficiently large integers, then the Hilbert polynomial \(\Phi _{\mathcal{F},s}\) of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:hilbert_polynomial">1006</a> does: \(\Phi _{\mathcal{F},s}(m) = h_{\mathcal{F},s}(m)\) for all \(m \gg 0\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:3398:  <p> Let \(\Psi \in \mathbb {Q}[\lambda ]\) agree with \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) at all \(m {\gt} N\). MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:3562:  <p>[The Hilbert polynomial computes as the extracted numerator polynomial]    Suppose there are \(p \in \mathbb {Q}[X]\) and \(d, N \in \mathbb {N}\) with \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}(m) = [X^m]\bigl(p \cdot (1-X)^{-d}\bigr)\) for all \(m {\gt} N\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:ratHilb">1019</a>). Then the Hilbert polynomial of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:hilbert_polynomial">1006</a> is the polynomial extracted from the pair \((p, d)\) by <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:hilbertPoly_exists_mathlib">1013</a>: \(\Phi _{\mathcal{F},s} = \mathrm{hilbertPoly}\, p\, d\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:3574:  <p> By <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:hilbertPoly_exists_mathlib">1013</a> there is an \(N'\) with \((\mathrm{hilbertPoly}\, p\, d)(n) = [X^n](p\cdot (1-X)^{-d})\) for all \(n {\gt} N'\), so \(\mathrm{hilbertPoly}\, p\, d\) agrees with \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) at all \(m {\gt} \max (N, N')\). Both \(\Phi _{\mathcal{F},s}\) and \(\mathrm{hilbertPoly}\, p\, d\) therefore agree with \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) at all sufficiently large integers, and <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:hilbertPolynomial_unique">1026</a> gives \(\Phi _{\mathcal{F},s} = \mathrm{hilbertPoly}\, p\, d\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:3658:<p><em>Status.</em> The polynomial-extraction half of this theorem is formalized: uniqueness (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:hilbertPolynomial_unique">1026</a>) and the extraction of the unique polynomial from a rational Hilbert function (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:hilbertPoly_of_isRatHilb">1027</a>, <span class="ttfamily">Scheme.existsUnique_hilbertPolynomial_of_isRatHilb</span>) are sorry-free. The remaining input is the geometric finite-generation theorem <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:sectionGradedModule_fg">1012</a> (Serre), which feeds the rationality hypothesis through <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:gradedHilbertSerre_rational">1016</a>. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:3670:  <p> By <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:sectionGradedModule_fg">1012</a> the section graded module \(M(X_s, \mathcal{F}_s, L_s)\) is a finitely generated graded module over the Noetherian graded ring \(R(X_s, L_s)\), with finite-dimensional components and degree-zero part the field \(\kappa (s)\). Applying the abstract graded Hilbert–Serre rationality lemma (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:gradedHilbertSerre_rational">1016</a>) to the graded \(\kappa (s)\)-algebra \(R = R(X_s, L_s)\) and the finitely generated graded module \(M = M(X_s, \mathcal{F}_s, L_s)\) exhibits the graded Hilbert function \(m \mapsto \dim _{\kappa (s)} \Gamma (X_s, \mathcal{F}_s \otimes L_s^{\otimes m})\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:fiber_hilbert_function">1011</a>) as a rational Hilbert function of some order \(d\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:ratHilb">1019</a>): there are \(p \in \mathbb {Q}[X]\), \(d \in \mathbb {N}\) and an \(N\) with \(\dim _{\kappa (s)} \Gamma (X_s, \mathcal{F}_s \otimes L_s^{\otimes m}) = [X^m]\, (p \cdot (1 - X)^{-d})\) for \(m {\gt} N\). The extraction lemma <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:hilbertPoly_of_isRatHilb">1027</a> then yields a unique polynomial \(\Phi _{\mathcal{F},s} \in \mathbb {Q}[\lambda ]\) with \(\Phi _{\mathcal{F},s}(m) = \dim _{\kappa (s)} \Gamma (X_s, \mathcal{F}_s \otimes L_s^{\otimes m})\) for all \(m \gg 0\), as claimed. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:3676:<p>The power-series side of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:gradedHilbertSerre_rational">1016</a> is fully isolated in the \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}\) toolkit (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#subsec:isRatHilb">20.3.1</a>). What remains is the <em>graded-module</em> side of the Stacks 00K1 induction. Rather than build the kernel and cokernel of multiplication by a degree-one element as graded modules over a smaller quotient ring \(R/(x)\) – which would force a graded structure on a derived carrier – we range the induction over <em>pairs of homogeneous submodules of a single fixed ambient graded module</em> \(M\). A pair \((N, N')\) with \(N' \le N\) homogeneous submodules of \(M\) stands for the subquotient \(N/N'\); its ambient Hilbert function is the difference \(n \mapsto \dim _\kappa (N \cap M_n) - \dim _\kappa (N' \cap M_n)\). The class of such pairs, equipped with finitely many pairwise-commuting degree-one endomorphisms preserving \(N\) and \(N'\), is <em>closed</em> under the kernel and cokernel of one of those endomorphisms, both again presented as ambient subquotient pairs. Consequently no graded quotient ring, graded quotient module, or regrading of a subtype/quotient carrier is ever formed: every object that appears is an ambient family \(n \mapsto N_{\mathrm{aux}} \cap M_n\) of submodules of the fixed \(M\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:3677:<p>This subsection records that machinery as a thin layer over existing Mathlib scaffold: Mathlib already provides the notion of a homogeneous submodule (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:submodule_isHomogeneous_mathlib">1032</a>), the homogeneity of a span of homogeneous elements (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:ideal_homogeneous_span_mathlib">1033</a>), the degree-shift of multiplication by a homogeneous element (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isHomogeneousElem_graded_smul_mathlib">1036</a>), the rank–nullity identity (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:finrank_range_add_finrank_ker_mathlib">1034</a>), and the finite-generation transfer along a surjection (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:fg_restrictScalars_of_surjective_mathlib">1035</a>). What is supplied here is the internal direct-sum decomposition of a homogeneous submodule as an ambient family (the split \(G_1\)), the subquotient Hilbert data, the kernel/cokernel closure, the degreewise difference identity, the ambient finiteness transfer, and the induction itself. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:3694:    <a class="icon proof" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:submodule_isHomogeneous_mathlib">#</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:3720:  <p>   <i class="itshape">Provided by Mathlib (<span class="ttfamily">Mathlib.RingTheory.GradedAlgebra.Homogeneous.Submodule</span>).</i> Let \(R = \bigoplus _n R_n\) be a graded ring and \(M = \bigoplus _n M_n\) an internally graded \(R\)-module. A submodule \(p \subseteq M\) is <em>homogeneous</em> when it is closed under taking homogeneous components: \(m \in p\) implies each graded piece \(\mathrm{proj}_n(m) \in p\). Equivalently \(p = \bigoplus _n (p \cap M_n)\) as a set. Mathlib bundles this into a homogeneous submodule type providing order and extensionality structure; the ambient internal direct-sum decomposition \(p = \bigoplus _n (M_n \cap p)\) is supplied by the split \(G_1\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_homogeneousSubmodule_iSupIndep">1044</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_homogeneousSubmodule_iSup_eq">1045</a>). </p>

Then the ideal \(\mathrm{span}\, s\) is a homogeneous ideal. In particular, for \(x \in R_1\) the principal ideal \((x)\) is homogeneous, hence \(xM\) and the auxiliary submodule \(N' + x \cdot N\) are homogeneous; this homogeneity feeds the kernel/cokernel closure (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_ker_coker">1065</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:3856:  <p>   <i class="itshape">Provided by Mathlib (<span class="ttfamily">Mathlib.RingTheory.Finiteness.Basic</span>).</i> Let \(\varphi : R \to A\) be a surjective ring homomorphism and \(M\) an \(A\)-module that is finitely generated when viewed as an \(R\)-module via \(\varphi \). Then \(M\) is finitely generated as an \(A\)-module. Applied to the surjection \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}] \twoheadrightarrow \kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-2}]\) killing the endomorphism \(x = t_{r-1}\) that annihilates the two subquotients, this transfers their finite generation down one generator (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_finite_transfer">1080</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:3900:  <p>   <i class="itshape">Provided by Mathlib (<span class="ttfamily">Mathlib.Algebra.GradedMulAction</span>).</i> Let \(\mathcal{A}\) be a graded family acting on a graded family \(\mathcal{M}\) via a graded scalar multiplication. If \(a \in R\) is homogeneous of degree \(i\) – in particular \(x \in R_1\) – then for \(m \in M_n\) one has \(a \cdot m \in M_{i+n}\). This is the degree-shifting property that makes \(xM\) a homogeneous submodule (with degree-\((n+1)\) part \(x \cdot M_n\)) and that underlies the ambient identity \(x \cdot N \cap M_{n+1} = x \cdot (N \cap M_n)\) used in the subquotient closure (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_ker_coker">1065</a>) and difference identity (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_degreewise_diff">1067</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:3944:  <p>   <i class="itshape">Provided by Mathlib (<span class="ttfamily">Mathlib.Algebra.Algebra.Subalgebra.Lattice</span>).</i> Let \(R\) be a commutative semiring and \(A\) an \(R\)-algebra, possibly noncommutative. If \(s \subseteq A\) is a set of pairwise-commuting elements (\(a b = b a\) for all \(a, b \in s\)), then the \(R\)-subalgebra \(\mathrm{adjoin}_R(s)\) generated by \(s\) has commutative multiplication; the commutative-ring structure on it follows. Applied to the \(r\) pairwise-commuting degree-raising endomorphisms \(x_0, \dots , x_{r-1} \in \operatorname {End}_\kappa (M)\), it yields a <em>commutative</em> \(\kappa \)-subalgebra \(A = \mathrm{adjoin}_\kappa \{ x_0, \dots , x_{r-1}\}  \subseteq \operatorname {End}_\kappa (M)\); the polynomial action of \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\) on \(M\) factors through this commutative \(A\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_finite_transfer">1080</a>). </p>

Form the two new pairs of homogeneous submodules of \(M\) </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:5804:  <p> <em>Homogeneity.</em> The preimage \(x^{-1}(N')\) is homogeneous: if \(m = \sum _n \mathrm{proj}_n(m)\) with \(x \cdot m \in N'\), then since \(x\) raises degree by one (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isHomogeneousElem_graded_smul_mathlib">1036</a>) the components \(x \cdot \mathrm{proj}_n(m) \in \mathcal{M}_{n+1}\) lie in distinct degrees, and homogeneity of \(N'\) (split \(G_1\), <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_homogeneousSubmodule_iSup_eq">1045</a>) forces each \(x \cdot \mathrm{proj}_n(m) \in N'\), i.e. \(\mathrm{proj}_n(m) \in x^{-1}(N')\). Thus \(N \cap x^{-1}(N')\) is an intersection of homogeneous submodules, hence homogeneous. The image \(x \cdot N\) is homogeneous with degree-\((n+1)\) piece \(x \cdot (N \cap \mathcal{M}_n)\) by <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isHomogeneousElem_graded_smul_mathlib">1036</a>, and a sum of homogeneous submodules is homogeneous (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:ideal_homogeneous_span_mathlib">1033</a> applied at the module level), so \(N' + x \cdot N\) is homogeneous. The inclusions \(N' \le N \cap x^{-1}(N')\) (as \(x \cdot N' \subseteq N'\)) and \(N' + x \cdot N \le N\) (as \(N' \le N\) and \(x \cdot N \subseteq N\)) are immediate. In the language of the ambient homogeneity calculus, this paragraph is exactly: \(x^{-1}(N')\) is homogeneous (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_comap_isHomogeneous">1051</a>), \(x \cdot N\) is homogeneous (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_map_isHomogeneous">1052</a>), and the homogeneous lattice is closed under intersection (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_inf_isHomogeneous">1053</a>) and sum (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_sup_isHomogeneous">1054</a>). </p>

Let \(h_K\) and \(h_C\) be the Hilbert functions of the kernel and cokernel subquotients \(K = (N \cap x^{-1}(N'),\,  N')\) and \(C = (N,\,  N' + x \cdot N)\) of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_ker_coker">1065</a>. Then for every \(n\) </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:5964:<p> Writing \(Q_n = (N \cap \mathcal{M}_n)/(N' \cap \mathcal{M}_n)\) for the degree-\(n\) piece of \(N/N'\) (so \(\dim _\kappa Q_n = h_M(n)\)), multiplication by \(x\) is a \(\kappa \)-linear map \(x : Q_n \to Q_{n+1}\) with \(\ker (x : Q_n \to Q_{n+1})\) the degree-\(n\) piece of \(K\) and \(Q_{n+1}/\operatorname {im} x\) the degree-\((n+1)\) piece of \(C\); the identity is then the degreewise rank–nullity difference \(D_5\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_degreewise_finrank_diff">1085</a>). Specialising to \((N, N') = (\top , \bot )\) recovers the classical \(0 \to \mathcal{M}_n \xrightarrow {x} \mathcal{M}_{n+1} \to \mathcal{M}_{n+1}/x\mathcal{M}_n \to 0\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:5976:  <p> Since \(N' \le N\) are homogeneous, the split \(G_1\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_homogeneousSubmodule_iSup_eq">1045</a>) identifies the degree-\(n\) piece of \(N/N'\) with \(Q_n = (N \cap \mathcal{M}_n)/(N' \cap \mathcal{M}_n)\), a finite-dimensional \(\kappa \)-vector space of dimension \(h_M(n)\). Because \(x\) raises degree by one and preserves \(N\) and \(N'\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isHomogeneousElem_graded_smul_mathlib">1036</a>), it induces a \(\kappa \)-linear map \(x : Q_n \to Q_{n+1}\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:5977:<p><em>Kernel.</em> A class \([m] \in Q_n\) (with \(m \in N \cap \mathcal{M}_n\)) lies in \(\ker (x : Q_n \to Q_{n+1})\) iff \(x \cdot m \in N' \cap \mathcal{M}_{n+1}\), i.e. iff \(m \in (N \cap x^{-1}(N')) \cap \mathcal{M}_n\). Hence \(\ker (x : Q_n \to Q_{n+1}) = \bigl((N \cap x^{-1}(N')) \cap \mathcal{M}_n\bigr)/(N' \cap \mathcal{M}_n)\) is exactly the degree-\(n\) piece of \(K\), of dimension \(h_K(n)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_ker_coker">1065</a>). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:5978:<p><em>Cokernel.</em> The image of \(x : Q_n \to Q_{n+1}\) is \(\bigl(x \cdot (N \cap \mathcal{M}_n) + (N' \cap \mathcal{M}_{n+1})\bigr)/(N' \cap \mathcal{M}_{n+1})\). Using the ambient identity \((N' + x \cdot N) \cap \mathcal{M}_{n+1} = (N' \cap \mathcal{M}_{n+1}) + x \cdot (N \cap \mathcal{M}_n)\) – which is the ambient distributive law (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_sup_inf_degree_eq">1056</a>) applied to \(P = N'\), \(Q = x \cdot N\), combined with the ambient image identity \((x \cdot N) \cap \mathcal{M}_{n+1} = x \cdot (N \cap \mathcal{M}_n)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_map_inf_degree_eq">1055</a>) – the cokernel \(Q_{n+1}/\operatorname {im} x = (N \cap \mathcal{M}_{n+1})/\bigl((N' + x \cdot N) \cap \mathcal{M}_{n+1}\bigr)\) is the degree-\((n+1)\) piece of \(C\), of dimension \(h_C(n+1)\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:5988:<p>The finiteness condition of a subquotient datum (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientHilb">1046</a>) and its transfer down one generator (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_finite_transfer">1080</a>) are phrased over the <em>free</em> polynomial ring \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}] = \operatorname {MvPolynomial}(\{ 0, \dots , r-1\} , \kappa )\). The following blocks build the action of that ring on the ambient module \(M\) from the \(r\) pairwise-commuting degree-raising endomorphisms \(t_i\), keeping every carrier an ambient submodule of \(M\). The free polynomial ring – rather than the subalgebra \(\mathrm{adjoin}_\kappa \{ t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}\}  \subseteq \operatorname {End}_\kappa (M)\) – is used precisely so the inductive transfer has the ring surjection \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}] \twoheadrightarrow \kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-2}]\) available (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_finite_transfer">1080</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:6241:  <p>[Polynomial-ring module structure on \(M\)]    The <em>polynomial-module structure</em> is the \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\)-module structure on \(M\) obtained by restricting scalars along \(\mathrm{polyEndHom}(t)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyEndHom">1068</a>): a polynomial \(p\) acts on \(m \in M\) by \(p \cdot m = \mathrm{polyEndHom}(t)(p)(m)\). This is the module over the free polynomial ring on which the ambient subquotient induction’s finiteness condition is measured. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:6438:  <p>[Polynomial-ring submodule from a \(t\)-stable submodule]    Let \(N \subseteq M\) be a \(\kappa \)-submodule that is stable under each \(t_i\) (\(t_i \cdot N \subseteq N\)). Then \(N\), with the <em>same</em> ambient carrier, is a \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\)-submodule of \(M\) for the polynomial-module structure (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyModule">1071</a>). Stability under the action of an arbitrary polynomial follows by induction on monomials: constants act as scalars (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyModule_C_smul">1073</a>) and multiplication by \(X_i\) acts as \(t_i\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyModule_X_smul">1072</a>), both of which preserve \(N\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:6443:<p>The ambient finiteness transfer (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_finite_transfer">1080</a>) factors the polynomial action of the larger ring through a surjection onto the smaller one. The following blocks build that surjection and the semilinearity identity it rests on, and record the two elementary finiteness manipulations (shrinking a numerator, enlarging a denominator) used to feed the kernel and cokernel constructors. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:6720:  <p>[Shrinking the numerator preserves finiteness]    Let \(N_1 \le N_2\) and \(P'\) be \(\kappa \)-submodules of \(M\), each stable under the commuting family \(t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}\), and suppose the subquotient \(N_2/P'\) is finite over \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyModule">1071</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polySubmodule">1074</a>). Then \(N_1/P'\) is also finite over \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\). Indeed the inclusion \(N_1 \subseteq N_2\) induces an injective \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\)-linear map \(N_1/P' \hookrightarrow N_2/P'\); since \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\) is Noetherian (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:mvPolynomial_isNoetherianRing_fin_mathlib">1042</a>), the finite module \(N_2/P'\) is Noetherian (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isNoetherian_of_isNoetherianRing_of_finite_mathlib">1043</a>), so its submodule \(N_1/P'\) is finite (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:module_finite_of_injective_mathlib">1039</a>). This supplies the finiteness witness of the kernel constructor (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientDatum_ker">1083</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:6789:  <p>[Enlarging the denominator preserves finiteness]    Let \(N\) and \(P_1 \le P_2\) be \(\kappa \)-submodules of \(M\), each stable under the commuting family \(t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}\), and suppose the subquotient \(N/P_1\) is finite over \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyModule">1071</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polySubmodule">1074</a>). Then \(N/P_2\) is also finite over \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\). Indeed the inclusion \(P_1 \subseteq P_2\) gives a surjection \(N/P_1 \twoheadrightarrow N/P_2\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:submodule_liftQ_mathlib">1040</a>), and finiteness transfers along it (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:module_finite_of_surjective_mathlib">1038</a>). This supplies the finiteness witness of the cokernel constructor (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientDatum_coker">1084</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:6880:  <p>[Abstract single-pair finiteness transfer down one variable]    Let \(t_0, \dots , t_r\) be pairwise-commuting \(\kappa \)-linear endomorphisms of \(M\), and let \(P' \le P\) be \(\kappa \)-submodules of \(M\), each stable under every \(t_i\). Suppose the last endomorphism \(x = t_r\) carries \(P\) into \(P'\) (\(x \cdot P \subseteq P'\)), and that the subquotient \(P/P'\) is finite over the free polynomial ring \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r]\) for the polynomial-module structure of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyModule">1071</a> (with carriers the ambient \(t\)-stable submodules \(\mathrm{polySubmodule}\, P\), \(\mathrm{polySubmodule}\, P'\), <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polySubmodule">1074</a>). Then \(P/P'\) is finite over \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\) for the reduced family \((t_0, \dots , t_{r-1})\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:6881:<p>This is the abstract single-pair transfer: it does not mention the kernel/cokernel pairs, but is the engine applied to each of them by the kernel and cokernel constructors (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientDatum_ker">1083</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientDatum_coker">1084</a>). Because the last variable annihilates the subquotient, the \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r]\)-action factors through the last-variable surjection \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r] \twoheadrightarrow \kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\), which is what makes the transfer drop one variable. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:6893:  <p> Write \(\sigma = \mathrm{lastVarAlgHom} : \kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r] \twoheadrightarrow \kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\) for the surjective ring homomorphism sending the last variable to \(0\) and each earlier variable \(X_i\) (\(i {\lt} r\)) to \(X_i\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_lastVarAlgHom">1075</a>). Consider the map on numerators </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:6897:<p> where the source carries the \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r]\)-module structure and the target the reduced \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\)-module structure (both with the same ambient carrier \(P\), <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polySubmodule">1074</a>). The mod-\(P'\) semilinearity identity (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyEndHom_lastVar_sub_mem">1077</a>) – acting by \(s\) through the full family and acting by \(\sigma (s)\) through the reduced family agree modulo \(P'\), precisely because \(x = t_r\) carries \(P\) into \(P'\) – says exactly that \(g\) is \(\sigma \)-semilinear. The map \(g\) is surjective (it is the quotient projection on the common carrier), and it kills the denominator \(\mathrm{polySubmodule}\, P'\), so it descends through that submodule (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:submodule_liftQ_mathlib">1040</a>) to a surjective \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\)-linear map </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:6901:<p> from the \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r]\)-finite subquotient onto the reduced one. Finiteness transfers along this surjection (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:module_finite_of_surjective_mathlib">1038</a>), giving finiteness of \(P/P'\) over \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:6902:<p><em>Why the free polynomial ring.</em> The smaller ring must be the <em>free</em> polynomial ring \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\), not the subalgebra \(\mathrm{adjoin}_\kappa \{ t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}\}  \subseteq \operatorname {End}_\kappa (M)\): relations among the endomorphisms inside \(\operatorname {End}_\kappa (M)\) would obstruct the polynomial-ring surjection \(\sigma \) that the scalar transfer requires (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:fg_restrictScalars_of_surjective_mathlib">1035</a>). Keeping free polynomial rings at every step keeps \(\sigma \) – and hence the transfer – available throughout. Everything is finite generation of ambient submodules of the fixed \(M\) and their quotients. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:6907:<p>The kernel/cokernel closure (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_ker_coker">1065</a>) and the abstract finiteness transfer (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_finite_transfer">1080</a>) are bundled into two constructors that take a length-\((r+1)\) subquotient datum to the length-\(r\) kernel and cokernel data consumed by the induction. The two stability lemmas below first record that the new pairs are stable under the <em>whole</em> endomorphism family (not merely the reduced one), which is what lets the over-\(\kappa [t_0,\dots ,t_r]\) finiteness inputs be stated before the variable is dropped. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:6967:  <p>[The kernel pair’s lower module is stable under the full family]    Let \((N, N')\) be a length-\((r+1)\) subquotient datum (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientHilb">1046</a>) with endomorphisms \(t_0, \dots , t_r\) and \(x = t_r\). Then the kernel pair’s lower module \(N \cap x^{-1}(N')\) is stable under <em>every</em> \(t_i\) (\(0 \le i \le r\)), not only the reduced family: each \(t_i\) preserves \(N\) and preserves the preimage \(x^{-1}(N')\) because it commutes with \(x\) and preserves \(N'\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_comap_map_le_of_commute">1063</a>). This full stability is what allows the kernel subquotient’s finiteness to be measured over \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r]\) before the transfer drops the last variable. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7030:  <p>[The cokernel pair’s upper module is stable under the full family]    Under the same hypotheses, the cokernel pair’s upper module \(N' + x \cdot N\) is stable under every \(t_i\) (\(0 \le i \le r\)): each \(t_i\) preserves \(N'\) and preserves the image \(x \cdot N\) because it commutes with \(x\) and preserves \(N\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_map_map_le_of_commute">1064</a>), and a map preserves a sum of preserved submodules. This full stability supports the over-\(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r]\) finiteness input of the cokernel constructor. </p>

Its non-finiteness fields are supplied by the ambient kernel calculus: homogeneity of \(N \cap x^{-1}(N')\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_ker_isHomogeneous">1057</a>), the nesting \(N' \le N \cap x^{-1}(N')\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_ker_le">1059</a>), and stability under the reduced family (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_ker_stable_full">1081</a>). The finiteness witness is obtained by first shrinking the numerator from \(N\) to \(N \cap x^{-1}(N')\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyQuot_finite_of_le_numerator">1078</a>) to get \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r]\)-finiteness of the kernel subquotient, then transferring down one variable (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_finite_transfer">1080</a>), valid because \(x\) annihilates the kernel subquotient (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_ker_annihilate">1061</a>). MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7289:  <p> By rank–nullity (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:finrank_range_add_finrank_ker_mathlib">1034</a>), \(\dim _\kappa V = \dim _\kappa (\ker \varphi ) + \dim _\kappa (\operatorname {range} \varphi )\), so \(\dim _\kappa (\operatorname {range}\varphi ) = \dim _\kappa V - \dim _\kappa (\ker \varphi )\). By additivity on the short exact sequence \(0 \to \operatorname {range}\varphi \to W \to W/\operatorname {range}\varphi \to 0\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:finrank_ses_additive_mathlib">1014</a>), \(\dim _\kappa (W/\operatorname {range}\varphi ) = \dim _\kappa W - \dim _\kappa (\operatorname {range}\varphi ) = \dim _\kappa W - \dim _\kappa V + \dim _\kappa (\ker \varphi )\). Rearranging gives \(\dim _\kappa W - \dim _\kappa V = \dim _\kappa (W/\operatorname {range}\varphi ) - \dim _\kappa (\ker \varphi )\). The degreewise application identifies \(\ker (x : \mathcal{M}_n \to \mathcal{M}_{n+1})\) and \(\mathcal{M}_{n+1}/\operatorname {range}(x : \mathcal{M}_n \to \mathcal{M}_{n+1})\) with the degree-\(n\) piece of the kernel subquotient and the degree-\((n+1)\) piece of the cokernel subquotient (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_degreewise_diff">1067</a>), the latter because the degree-\((n+1)\) graded piece of the homogeneous submodule \(x\mathcal{M}\) is exactly \(x \mathcal{M}_n\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isHomogeneousElem_graded_smul_mathlib">1036</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7333:  <p>[Base-case finiteness over the empty polynomial ring]   Let \(Q\) be a \(\kappa \)-vector space that is also a module over \(\operatorname {MvPolynomial}(\sigma , \kappa )\) for an <em>empty</em> index set \(\sigma \) – in particular \(\sigma = \{ 0, \dots , r-1\} \) with \(r = 0\) – in a way compatible with the \(\kappa \)-action (scalar tower). If \(Q\) is module-finite over \(\operatorname {MvPolynomial}(\sigma , \kappa )\), then \(Q\) is finite-dimensional over \(\kappa \). Indeed for empty \(\sigma \) the polynomial ring is \(\operatorname {MvPolynomial}(\sigma , \kappa ) \cong \kappa \), a finite \(\kappa \)-module, so finiteness of \(Q\) over it transfers to finiteness over \(\kappa \) along the scalar tower. This is the length-zero input to the ambient subquotient induction (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_isRatHilb">1089</a>): when \(r = 0\) the subquotient \(N/N'\) is a finite-dimensional \(\kappa \)-vector space, hence \(\mathrm{hilb}\) is eventually zero. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7475:  <p>[Base case: the length-zero subquotient Hilbert function vanishes eventually]    <i class="itshape">Source: [Stacks Project], Tag 00K1 (base case of the induction).</i> Let \((N, N')\) be a subquotient datum of length \(0\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientHilb">1046</a>): a homogeneous pair \(N' \le N\) of the fixed ambient graded module \(M = \bigoplus _n \mathcal{M}_n\) with <em>no</em> endomorphisms, whose finiteness witness says the subquotient \(Q_0 := N/N'\) is module-finite over \(\operatorname {MvPolynomial}(\varnothing , \kappa )\). Then the ambient Hilbert function vanishes eventually: there is \(K \in \mathbb {N}\) with \(\mathrm{hilb}(n) = 0\) for all \(n {\gt} K\). Consequently \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(\mathrm{hilb}, 0)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:ratHilb_ofEventuallyZero">1020</a>), which is the base case of the ambient subquotient induction (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_isRatHilb">1089</a>). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7487:  <p> Since the index set of variables is empty, \(\operatorname {MvPolynomial}(\varnothing , \kappa ) \cong \kappa \), so the finiteness witness makes the subquotient \(Q_0 = N/N'\) a <em>finite-dimensional</em> \(\kappa \)-vector space (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_finiteDimensional_of_mvPolynomial_isEmpty_finite">1086</a>). For each degree \(n\), composing the inclusion of the homogeneous piece \(N \cap \mathcal{M}_n \hookrightarrow N\) with the quotient projection \(N \twoheadrightarrow Q_0\) gives a \(\kappa \)-linear map \(\psi _n : N \cap \mathcal{M}_n \to Q_0\), \(m \mapsto [m]\), whose image is the class of the degree-\(n\) homogeneous piece inside the subquotient. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7488:<p><em>Step 1: independence of the images.</em> The family \(\bigl(\operatorname {range}(\psi _n)\bigr)_{n}\) is \(\mathrm{iSupIndep}\) in \(Q_0\). The reason is the ambient direct-sum grading of \(M\): the homogeneous pieces \(\mathcal{M}_n\) form an independent family (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_homogeneousSubmodule_iSupIndep">1044</a>). An element of \(\bigsqcup _{j \ne n} \operatorname {range}(\psi _j)\) is a finite sum of classes of homogeneous elements of degrees \(j \ne n\); since \(N'\) is homogeneous, the degree-\(n\) homogeneous component of any representative of such a class lies in \(N'\), so the class has zero degree-\(n\) component in \(Q_0\). A nonzero class in \(\operatorname {range}(\psi _n)\), by contrast, is represented by a homogeneous element of degree \(n\) not in \(N'\), so has nonzero degree-\(n\) component. Comparing degree-\(n\) components forces the intersection \(\operatorname {range}(\psi _n) \cap \bigsqcup _{j \ne n} \operatorname {range}(\psi _j) = 0\); independence follows. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7489:<p><em>Step 2: finiteness of the support.</em> Because \(Q_0\) is finite-dimensional and the ranges \(\operatorname {range}(\psi _n)\) are independent, only finitely many of them are nonzero: the set \(\{ \, n : \operatorname {range}(\psi _n) \ne 0\, \} \) is finite (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:finite_ne_bot_of_iSupIndep_mathlib">1041</a>). In particular it is bounded above, by some \(K \in \mathbb {N}\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7494:<p> Thus \(\mathrm{hilb}\) is eventually zero, and <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:ratHilb_ofEventuallyZero">1020</a> gives \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(\mathrm{hilb}, 0)\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7601:  <p>[Rationality of the ambient subquotient Hilbert function]    <i class="itshape">Source: [Stacks Project], Tag 00K1 (induction on the number of degree-one generators).</i> Let \((N, N')\) be a subquotient datum of length \(r\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientHilb">1046</a>) with ambient Hilbert function \(\mathrm{hilb}\). Then \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(\mathrm{hilb}, r)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:ratHilb">1019</a>): the difference \(n \mapsto \dim _\kappa (N \cap \mathcal{M}_n) - \dim _\kappa (N' \cap \mathcal{M}_n)\) is, for \(n \gg 0\), the coefficient sequence of a rational series \(p \cdot (1 - X)^{-r}\) with \(p \in \mathbb {Q}[X]\). The induction is on the length \(r\), and every object that appears is an ambient pair of homogeneous submodules of the fixed graded module \(M\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7614:<p><em>Base case \(r = 0\).</em> A length-zero datum has a finiteness witness making the subquotient \(N/N'\) a finite-dimensional \(\kappa \)-vector space (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_finiteDimensional_of_mvPolynomial_isEmpty_finite">1086</a>); its degreewise images form an independent family inside that finite-dimensional space, so only finitely many are nonzero and \(\mathrm{hilb}(n) = 0\) for \(n \gg 0\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_base_eventuallyZero">1088</a>). By <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:ratHilb_ofEventuallyZero">1020</a> an eventually-zero function is rational of order \(0\), giving \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(\mathrm{hilb}, 0)\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7615:<p><em>Inductive step \(r \ge 1\).</em> Set \(x = t_{r-1}\). By the kernel/cokernel closure (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_ker_coker">1065</a>) the kernel subquotient \(K = (N \cap x^{-1}(N'),\,  N')\) and the cokernel subquotient \(C = (N,\,  N' + x \cdot N)\) are subquotient data of length \(r-1\), assembled by the kernel and cokernel constructors (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientDatum_ker">1083</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientDatum_coker">1084</a>) whose finiteness witnesses come from the abstract finiteness transfer (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_finite_transfer">1080</a>). The induction hypothesis applied to \(K\) and \(C\) gives \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(h_K, r-1)\) and \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(h_C, r-1)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:ratHilb">1019</a>). By the degreewise difference identity (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_degreewise_diff">1067</a>), </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7619:<p> Feeding \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(h_C, r-1)\), \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(h_K, r-1)\) and this difference identity into the inductive-step engine (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:ratHilb_ofDiffEq">1025</a>) yields \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(\mathrm{hilb}, r)\). (The common order \(r-1\) for \(h_C\) and \(h_K\) is arranged, if necessary, by raising the lower one with <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:ratHilb_bump">1021</a>.) This completes the induction. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7625:<p>The Quot functor (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:quot_functor">1126</a>) and the Grassmannian (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:grassmannian_scheme">1164</a>) classify quotient sheaves subject to two geometric conditions: a coherent quotient must have <em>schematic support proper over the base</em>, and the Grassmannian’s quotients must be <em>locally free of a fixed rank</em>. This section introduces both predicates. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7670:<p><em>Well-definedness on basic opens.</em> The coherence condition for an ideal sheaf requires that, for an affine open \(U\) and \(f \in \mathcal{O}_X(U)\), the section \(\mathrm{Ann}(\mathcal{F})(U)\) restricts correctly to the basic open \(D(f) \subseteq U\), i.e. that \(\mathrm{Ann}_{\mathcal{O}_X(D(f))}(\mathcal{F}(D(f)))\) is the extension of \(\mathrm{Ann}_{\mathcal{O}_X(U)}(\mathcal{F}(U))\) along the localization map \(\mathcal{O}_X(U) \to \mathcal{O}_X(D(f))\). This is exactly where the two hypotheses enter. The bridge <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen">1247</a> supplies, for a quasi-coherent finite-type \(\mathcal{F}\), that \(\mathcal{O}_X(D(f)) = (\mathcal{O}_X(U))_f\) and that the restriction \(\mathcal{F}(U) \to \mathcal{F}(D(f))\) exhibits \(\mathcal{F}(D(f))\) as the localized module \((\mathrm{powers}\, f)^{-1} \mathcal{F}(U)\); the algebra engine <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:annihilator_localization_eq_map">1094</a> then yields, using that \(\mathcal{F}(U)\) is finitely generated, the required identity \(\mathrm{Ann}_{(\mathcal{O}_X(U))_f}\bigl((\mathrm{powers}\, f)^{-1} \mathcal{F}(U)\bigr) = \mathrm{Ann}_{\mathcal{O}_X(U)}(\mathcal{F}(U)) \cdot (\mathcal{O}_X(U))_f\). Thus the local annihilators are compatible with basic-open restriction, which is the patching datum that makes \(\mathrm{Ann}(\mathcal{F})\) a well-defined ideal sheaf. The finite-type hypothesis is genuinely required: without finite generation of \(\mathcal{F}(U)\) the annihilator need not commute with localization, and the local data fail to patch. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:7827:  <p> The family \(I(V) := \mathrm{Ann}_{\mathcal{O}_X(V)}(\mathcal{F}(V))\), indexed by the affine opens of \(X\), satisfies the basic-open coherence required of an ideal sheaf: for an affine open \(V\) and \(f \in \mathcal{O}_X(V)\), the restriction \(\mathcal{O}_X(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(D(f))\) is the localization away from \(f\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isLocalization_basicOpen_mathlib">1093</a>), the section restriction \(\mathcal{F}(V) \to \mathcal{F}(D(f))\) is the corresponding module localization (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen">1247</a>), and — because \(\mathcal{F}(V)\) is finitely generated — the annihilator commutes with this localization (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:annihilator_localization_eq_map">1094</a>): \(I(D(f)) = I(V) \cdot \mathcal{O}_X(D(f))\). Hence \(I\) is itself an ideal sheaf. Since \(\mathrm{Ann}(\mathcal{F})\) is by definition the largest ideal sheaf whose affine-open values are contained in the family \(I\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:modules_annihilator">1090</a>), and \(I\) is such an ideal sheaf, maximality gives \(I(U) \subseteq \mathrm{Ann}(\mathcal{F})(U)\) for every affine \(U\); the reverse inclusion is <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_annihilator_ideal_le">1091</a>. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:8028:  <p>   <i class="itshape">Provided by Mathlib (<span class="ttfamily">Mathlib.Topology.Sheaves.SheafCondition.UniqueGluing</span>).</i> Let \(F\) be a sheaf on a topological space, \(V\) an open, and \(\{ U_i\} \) a family of opens with \(\bigsqcup _i U_i = V\). If two sections \(s, t \in F(V)\) have equal restrictions \(s|_{U_i} = t|_{U_i}\) for every \(i\), then \(s = t\). This separatedness over a cover is the uniqueness half of the sheaf condition; it discharges the \(\mathrm{exists\_ of\_ eq}\) obligation (a global section vanishing on \(D(f)\) is killed by a power of \(f\)) and the final “conclude on \(D(f)\)” step of the cover-form descent (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:section_localization_descent_of_cover">1112</a>). </p>
