MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:8838:  <p>[The Grothendieck-slice restriction equals the geometric restriction (gap1, C)]    <i class="itshape">The one lemma that must touch the Grothendieck slice site; everything downstream of it is geometric.</i> Let \(X\) be a scheme and \(U \subseteq X\) an open. The <em>abstract Grothendieck-slice</em> restriction \(M.\mathrm{over}\, U\) — an object of the category of sheaves of modules over the sliced structure sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_X.\mathrm{over}\, U\) on the slice site \(J.\mathrm{over}\, U\) — is canonically isomorphic to the <em>geometric</em> restriction \((\mathrm{restrictFunctor}\, U.\iota ).\mathrm{obj}\, M\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_restrictFunctor_mathlib">1098</a>), equivalently to the pullback \(U.\iota ^{*} M\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_mathlib">1099</a>), as a sheaf of modules on the small Zariski site of the open subscheme \(U.\mathrm{toScheme}\). The isomorphism is induced by the equivalence of sites \(J.\mathrm{over}\, U \simeq \mathrm{Opens}(U.\mathrm{toScheme})\) coming from the opens functor of the open immersion \(U.\iota \), under which the sliced sheaf of rings \(\mathcal{O}_X.\mathrm{over}\, U\) corresponds to the structure sheaf of \(U.\mathrm{toScheme}\). For \(X = \operatorname{Spec}R\) and \(U = D(r)\) a basic open, the target category is \((\operatorname{Spec}R_r).\mathrm{Modules}\) under the affine identification \(D(r) \cong \operatorname{Spec}R_r\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isLocalization_basicOpen_mathlib">1093</a>). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:8851:<p><em>Step 1 (topological layer — done).</em> The opens functor of the open immersion \(U.\iota \) realizes the slice of the opens site of \(X\) over \(U\) as the opens site of the subspace \(U\); on sheaf categories this is the equivalence \(\mathrm{Sheaf}(J_X|_U,\, A) \simeq \mathrm{Sheaf}(J_U,\, A)\) of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:overEquivalence_sheafCongr">1107</a>, for every target category \(A\). This is the topos-theoretic layer, assembled from the cocontinuity/continuity of both legs of \(\mathrm{Opens.overEquivalence}\, U\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:opens_overEquivalence_mathlib">1100</a>). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:8852:<p><em>Step 2 (geometric ring-sheaf identification — the current obstacle).</em> Identify the sliced structure sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_X.\mathrm{over}\, U\) with the structure sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_{U}\) of the open subscheme \(U.\mathrm{toScheme}\), transported across the \(\mathrm{RingCat}\)-valued instance of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:overEquivalence_sheafCongr">1107</a>; this is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings. The bridge is the factorization of the opens functor of the immersion, </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:8856:<p> under which the structure-sheaf comparison reduces to the standard open-immersion structure-sheaf identifications; recall that \(\mathrm{restrictFunctor}\, U.\iota \) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_restrictFunctor_mathlib">1098</a>) is precisely pushforward along \(U.\iota .\mathrm{opensFunctor}\). This ring-sheaf identification is the remaining geometric obstacle. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:8857:<p><em>Step 3 (lift to modules).</em> Given the step-2 identification of the underlying ring sheaves and the continuity of both legs (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:overEquivalence_functor_isContinuous">1105</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:overEquivalence_inverse_isContinuous">1106</a>), lift the sheaf-of-rings comparison to an equivalence of categories of sheaves of modules via \(\mathrm{pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence}\) (<a href="chap-Cohomology_CechHigherDirectImage.html#lem:pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence_mathlib">253</a>). Under this equivalence the sliced module \(M.\mathrm{over}\, U\) corresponds to the geometric restriction \((\mathrm{restrictFunctor}\, U.\iota ).\mathrm{obj}\, M\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:8858:<p><em>Step 4 (compose).</em> Compose with \(\mathrm{restrictFunctorIsoPullback}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_mathlib">1099</a>) to land the isomorphism \(M.\mathrm{over}\, U \cong M.\mathrm{restrict}\, U.\iota \cong U.\iota ^{*}M\). The two sides live a priori in different module categories, so the literal Lean statement of \(\mathrm{overRestrictIso}\) is phrased through the step-3 equivalence functor; for \(X = \operatorname{Spec}R\) and \(U = D(r)\) the target is \((\operatorname{Spec}R_r).\mathrm{Modules}\) under \(D(r) \cong \operatorname{Spec}R_r\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isLocalization_basicOpen_mathlib">1093</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9031:  <p>    Let \(M\) be a sheaf of modules on \(\operatorname{Spec}R\) equipped with quasi-coherence data: an open cover \(\{ X_i\} \) of \(\operatorname{Spec}R\) together with, for each \(i\), a presentation of the slice restriction \(M.\mathrm{over}\, X_i\) — an exhibition of it as the cokernel of a map between coproducts of copies of the unit module. Let \(r \in R\) with \(D(r) \subseteq X_i\) for some \(i\), and let \(W := \iota _{X_i}^{-1}(D(r))\) be the corresponding affine open of the subscheme \(Z := X_i\). Then the restriction of \(M\) to \(D(r)\) — the pullback of \(M\) to \(Z\), then to \(W\), transported across the affine identification \(W \cong \operatorname{Spec}\Gamma (Z, W)\) — has invertible tilde–\(\Gamma \) counit (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib">1244</a>); that is, \(M|_{D(r)}\) is the tilde of its section module over \(\Gamma (Z, W) \cong R_r\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isLocalization_basicOpen_mathlib">1093</a>). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9043:  <p> <em>Step 1 (geometrize the datum).</em> The quasi-coherence datum supplies a presentation of the slice restriction \(M.\mathrm{over}\, X_i\). The slice-to-geometric equivalence (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:over_restrict_equiv">1108</a>) preserves colimits and carries the unit module to the unit module, so the image of this presentation, transported along the isomorphism of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:over_restrict_pullback_iso">1110</a>, is a presentation of the geometric pullback \(N := \iota _{X_i}^{*} M\) on the scheme \(Z\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9044:<p><em>Step 2 (restrict to \(W\)).</em> Restriction to the slice site over \(W\) again preserves colimits and the unit, so the global presentation of \(N\) slices to a presentation of \(N.\mathrm{over}\, W\); geometrizing across the slice-to-geometric equivalence at \(W\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:over_restrict_equiv">1108</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:over_restrict_pullback_iso">1110</a>) yields a presentation of the geometric restriction \(\iota _W^{*} N\) on the open subscheme \(W\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9045:<p><em>Step 3 (affine identification).</em> \(W\) is affine: \(D(r)\) is a basic open of the affine scheme \(\operatorname{Spec}R\), and its preimage under the open immersion \(\iota _{X_i}\) is again affine because \(D(r)\) is contained in the immersion’s range. Pull the presentation back across the isomorphism \(W \cong \operatorname{Spec}\Gamma (Z, W)\): the pullback of sheaves of modules along an isomorphism of schemes (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_pullback_mathlib">1097</a>) preserves colimits, being a left adjoint, and carries the unit module to the unit module, since the induced functor on opens sites is an equivalence. This lands a global presentation of the transported module on the affine scheme \(\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma (Z, W)\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9046:<p><em>Step 4 (a presented module on \(\operatorname{Spec}S\) is a tilde).</em> Let \(P\) be a sheaf of modules on \(\operatorname{Spec}S\) with a presentation \(\mathcal{O}^{\oplus J} \to \mathcal{O}^{\oplus K} \to P \to 0\). The map of coproducts of units corresponds under the tilde–\(\Gamma \) adjunction (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib">1244</a>) to a map of free modules \(S^{\oplus J} \to S^{\oplus K}\), because \(\mathcal{O}^{\oplus K}\) is the tilde of \(S^{\oplus K}\) and the unit of the adjunction is an isomorphism. Since the tilde functor preserves cokernels (it is a left adjoint), \(P\) is isomorphic to the tilde of the cokernel of that module map. Finally, a module isomorphic to a tilde has invertible counit: on a tilde \(\widetilde{N}\) the triangle identity of the adjunction shows the counit is inverse to the tilde of the unit isomorphism \(N \cong \Gamma (\widetilde{N}, \top )\), and invertibility of the counit transports across any isomorphism of modules by naturality. Applying this to the transported module of Step 3 concludes. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9133:<p><em>Torsion.</em> Let \(x \in \Gamma (M, \top )\) restrict to \(0\) on \(D(f)\); we find \(n\) with \(f^n \cdot x = 0\) (applied to a difference \(x_1 - x_2\), this is the uniqueness condition). For each \(r \in t\), the restriction \(x|_{D(r)}\) restricts to \(0\) on \(D(f) \cap D(r)\) (functoriality of restriction through \(D(f)\)); the localization datum at \(U = D(r)\) then provides \(k_r\) with \(f^{k_r} \cdot x|_{D(r)} = 0\). Take \(n := \max _{r \in t} k_r\); then \((f^n \cdot x)|_{D(r)} = f^{\, n-k_r} \cdot \bigl(f^{k_r} \cdot x|_{D(r)}\bigr) = 0\) for every \(r\), and since the \(D(r)\) cover \(\operatorname{Spec}R\), sheaf separatedness (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:eq_of_locally_eq_mathlib">1096</a>) gives \(f^n \cdot x = 0\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9134:<p><em>Surjectivity.</em> Let \(y \in \Gamma (M, D(f))\); we find a global \(x\) and \(n\) with \(f^n \cdot y = x|_{D(f)}\). For each \(r \in t\), the localization datum at \(U = D(r)\) writes \(f^{m_r} \cdot y|_{D(f) \cap D(r)}\) as the restriction of a section \(b_r \in \Gamma (M, D(r))\); normalizing with the common exponent \(N := \max _r m_r\) (replace \(b_r\) by \(f^{\, N-m_r} \cdot b_r\)) we may assume \(b_r|_{D(f) \cap D(r)} = f^{N} \cdot y|_{D(f) \cap D(r)}\) for every \(r\). On a pairwise overlap \(D(r) \cap D(r')\) — an open contained in \(D(r)\) — the difference \(b_r - b_{r'}\) restricts to \(0\) on \(D(f) \cap D(r) \cap D(r')\), since both terms restrict to \(f^N \cdot y\) there; the localization datum at \(U = D(r) \cap D(r')\) provides a power \(f^{P_{r,r'}}\) killing the difference, and taking \(P := \max P_{r,r'}\) over the finitely many pairs, the family \(\{ f^P \cdot b_r\} _{r \in t}\) agrees on all overlaps. By the sheaf axiom (unique gluing over the finite cover \(\{ D(r)\} _{r \in t}\) of \(\operatorname{Spec}R\)) the family glues to a global section \(x \in \Gamma (M, \top )\). Finally \(x|_{D(f)} = f^{N+P} \cdot y\): the two sides agree on each member of the cover \(\{ D(f) \cap D(r)\} _{r \in t}\) of \(D(f)\), so they are equal by separatedness (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:eq_of_locally_eq_mathlib">1096</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9219:  <p> The proof of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:section_localization_descent_of_cover">1112</a> consults the localization datum only at the cover members \(U = D(r)\) (\(r \in t\)) and at their pairwise intersections \(U = D(r) \cap D(r') = D(r r')\) — all of them <em>basic</em> opens contained in a cover member. MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9224:<p>This subsection builds the geometric input of the gap1 keystone descent <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:section_localization_descent">1116</a>: the geometric <em>producer</em> <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:section_localization_hfr_basicOpen">1115</a> that manufactures, for a quasi-coherent \(M\) on \(\operatorname{Spec}R\) and a basic open \(D(s)\) inside a quasi-coherence cover member, the per-cover-element localization datum \(\mathrm{Hfr}\) the basic-open cover form <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:section_localization_descent_of_basicOpen_cover">1113</a> consumes. Then the section restriction </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9384:<p>Write \(M' := j^{*} M\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_pullback_mathlib">1097</a>). The per-element transport <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isIso_fromTildeΓ_basicOpen_of_quasicoherent">1111</a> gives invertibility of the tilde–\(\Gamma \) counit for the iterated pullback of \(M\) along the three legs of \(j\); pullback along a composite agrees with the composite of the pullbacks up to canonical natural isomorphism, and invertibility of the counit is invariant under isomorphism of modules (the essential image of the tilde functor is closed under isomorphism). Hence the counit of \(M'\) is invertible, and by <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isLocalizedModule_restrict_of_isIso_fromTildeΓ">1117</a>, for every \(f' \in S\) the restriction \(\Gamma (M', \top ) \to \Gamma (M', D(f'))\) is the localization at the powers of \(f'\) over \(S\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9386:<p>Since \(j\) is an open immersion, applying the section functor to the identification of the pullback with the restriction (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_mathlib">1099</a>) gives additive isomorphisms \(e_1 : \Gamma (M', \top ) \cong \Gamma \bigl(M, D(s)\bigr)\) and \(e_2 : \Gamma (M', D(f')) \cong \Gamma \bigl(M, D(f) \cap D(s)\bigr)\) which intertwine the two restriction maps (naturality of the identification in the open) and are \(\sigma \)-semilinear over the structure-sheaf comparisons: the action on the sections of the pullback is through the immersion’s section-ring isomorphism. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9387:<p>Finally apply the combiner <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isLocalizedModule_powers_transport">1114</a> with \(A := \Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}R, D(s))\) — an \(R\)-algebra through restriction of global sections — the isomorphism \(\sigma \), the elements \(f\) and \(f'\) (so that \(\sigma (f')\) is the image of \(f\) in \(A\)), the localization \(g := \bigl(\Gamma (M', \top ) \to \Gamma (M', D(f'))\bigr)\), the comparisons \(e_1, e_2\), and \(h := \bigl(\Gamma (M, D(s)) \to \Gamma (M, D(f) \cap D(s))\bigr)\): the conclusion is that \(h\) is the localization at the powers of \(f\) over \(R\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9460:  <p>    For a quasi-coherent sheaf of modules \(M\) on \(\operatorname{Spec}R\) and \(f \in R\), the section restriction \(\Gamma (M, \top ) \to \Gamma (M, D(f))\) exhibits the target as the localization \(\Gamma (M, \top )[1/f]\) over \(R\). This is the statement of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen">1247</a> at the affine open \(\top \) of \(\operatorname{Spec}R\), proved here by finite-cover descent — not through the affine equivalence of quasi-coherent modules with modules, which is instead <em>derived</em> from this lemma in <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:qcoh_affine_isIso_fromTildeΓ">1119</a>. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9472:  <p> Quasi-coherence provides a cover \(\{ X_i\} \) of \(\operatorname{Spec}R\) with per-member presentations. Refine it to a finite basic-open cover: the basic opens form a basis of \(\operatorname{Spec}R\), so every point has a basic-open neighbourhood contained in some \(X_i\); quasi-compactness of \(\operatorname{Spec}R\) extracts a finite family \(t \subseteq R\) with each \(D(r)\), \(r \in t\), contained in some \(X_i\), and covering is equivalent to \(t\) generating the unit ideal. For every basic open \(D(u)\) contained in some \(D(r)\) with \(r \in t\) — hence contained in a cover member \(X_i\) — the producer <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:section_localization_hfr_basicOpen">1115</a> supplies the localization datum at \(D(u)\). The basic-open cover form <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:section_localization_descent_of_basicOpen_cover">1113</a> then yields the conclusion. </p>

Then for every \(f \in R\) the section restriction \(\Gamma (M, \top ) \to \Gamma (M, D(f))\) exhibits the target as the localization of \(\Gamma (M, \top )\) at the powers of \(f\), over \(R\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9555:  <p> First let \(M = \widetilde{N}\) be a tilde. The unit \(N \to \Gamma (\widetilde{N}, \top )\) of the adjunction (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib">1244</a>) is an isomorphism, and the canonical map \(N \to \Gamma (\widetilde{N}, D(f))\) exhibits the target as the localized module \(N_f\) — the sections of a tilde over a basic open are the localization. MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:9642:<p>For the converse, write \(N := \Gamma (M, \top )\) and let \(\varepsilon : \widetilde{N} \to M\) be the counit. Fix \(f \in R\). The \(D(f)\)-component of \(\varepsilon \) is a map between two localizations of \(N\) at the powers of \(f\): the source \(\Gamma (\widetilde{N}, D(f))\) receives the canonical map from \(N\) (sections of a tilde over a basic open, as in the forward direction), and the target \(\Gamma (M, D(f))\) receives the restriction \(N = \Gamma (M, \top ) \to \Gamma (M, D(f))\), a localization by hypothesis. The component intertwines these two maps out of \(N\): the counit composed with the canonical section map is the section restriction, by the compatibility of the counit with the adjunction unit (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib">1244</a>) and naturality. A map between two localizations of the same module at the same multiplicative set commuting with the two localization maps is the canonical isomorphism between them, hence bijective. Thus \(\varepsilon \) is an isomorphism on every basic open. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:10454:<p><em>The basic opens of \(t\) cover \(V\).</em> Fix \(x \in V\). By <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:affine_finite_sections_nhds">1258</a> there is an affine open chart \(W\) with \(x \in W \subseteq V\) and \(\Gamma (\mathcal{F}, W)\) finite over \(\Gamma (X, W)\). Since the basic opens of the affine \(V\) form a basis of its topology, there is \(f \in \Gamma (X, V)\) with \(x \in D(f) \subseteq W\). Writing \(f|_W\) for the restriction of \(f\) to \(W\), one has \(D(f) = D(f|_W)\) as opens contained in \(W\); the restriction \(\Gamma (X, W) \to \Gamma (X, D(f))\) is the localization away from \(f|_W\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isLocalization_basicOpen_mathlib">1093</a>), and \(\Gamma (\mathcal{F}, W) \to \Gamma (\mathcal{F}, D(f))\) is the corresponding module localization (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen">1247</a>, applicable because a finitely presented module is quasi-coherent). The images of a finite generating set of \(\Gamma (\mathcal{F}, W)\) generate the localized module over the localized ring, so \(\Gamma (\mathcal{F}, D(f))\) is finite over \(\Gamma (X, D(f))\) and \(f \in t\), with \(x \in D(f)\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:10455:<p><em>Conclusion.</em> The basic opens \(D(f)\), \(f \in t\), cover the affine \(V\), so \(t\) generates the unit ideal of \(\Gamma (X, V)\). For each \(f \in t\) the restriction \(\Gamma (\mathcal{F}, V) \to \Gamma (\mathcal{F}, D(f))\) is the localization of \(\Gamma (\mathcal{F}, V)\) away from \(f\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen">1247</a>), with target a finite \(\Gamma (X, D(f)) = \Gamma (X, V)_f\)-module by membership in \(t\); <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:module_finite_of_localizationSpan_mathlib">1129</a> glues these into finiteness of \(\Gamma (\mathcal{F}, V)\) over \(\Gamma (X, V)\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:10514:<p><em>Pullback intertwines the multiplication endomorphisms.</em> For a morphism \(h : Z' \to Z\) one has \(h^*(w \cdot ) = (h^\sharp w) \cdot \) as endomorphisms of \(h^* \mathcal{M}\). Indeed, under the adjunction between \(h^*\) and \(h_*\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_pullback_mathlib">1097</a>) both sides transpose to morphisms \(\mathcal{M} \to h_* h^* \mathcal{M}\), and these transposes agree: the adjunction unit \(\eta : \mathcal{M} \to h_* h^* \mathcal{M}\) is a morphism of \(\mathcal{O}_Z\)-modules, and the \(\mathcal{O}_Z\)-module structure of \(h_* h^* \mathcal{M}\) is restriction of scalars along \(h^\sharp \), so both transposes send a section \(m\) over \(O \subseteq Z\) to \(\bigl(h^\sharp (w|_O)\bigr) \cdot \eta (m) = \bigl(w|_O\bigr) \cdot \eta (m)\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:10515:<p><em>On an affine scheme, killing global sections kills all sections.</em> Let \(Z\) be affine, \(\mathcal{M}\) quasi-coherent, and suppose \(w \cdot \Gamma (\mathcal{M}, Z) = 0\). On a basic open \(D(b)\) the restriction \(\Gamma (\mathcal{M}, Z) \to \Gamma (\mathcal{M}, D(b))\) is the localization away from \(b\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen">1247</a>); for \(y \in \Gamma (\mathcal{M}, D(b))\) there are \(n\) and \(m \in \Gamma (\mathcal{M}, Z)\) with \(b^n y = m|_{D(b)}\), whence \(b^n (w y) = w|_{D(b)} \cdot m|_{D(b)} = (w \cdot m)|_{D(b)} = 0\); since \(b\) acts invertibly on the localized sections, \(w y = 0\). A general open of \(Z\) is covered by basic opens and the abelian sheaf underlying \(\mathcal{M}\) is separated, so multiplication by (the restriction of) \(w\) kills all sections of \(\mathcal{M}\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:10516:<p><em>Conclusion.</em> Restrict \(\mathcal{F}\) to the affine open subscheme \(U\), i.e. form \(\iota _U^* \mathcal{F}\) for the open immersion \(\iota _U : U \to X\); it is quasi-coherent (<a href="chap-Cohomology_CechHigherDirectImage.html#lem:pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom">507</a>), and the global section \(r_0 \in \mathcal{O}_U(U)\) corresponding to \(r\) kills \(\Gamma (\iota _U^* \mathcal{F}, U) = \Gamma (\mathcal{F}, U)\). By the affine step, \(r_0 \cdot \) is the zero endomorphism of \(\iota _U^* \mathcal{F}\). Let \(h : V' \to U\) be the restriction of \(g'\), defined since \(V' \subseteq g'^{-1}(U)\); by the intertwining step \((h^\sharp r_0) \cdot \) is the zero endomorphism of \(h^* \iota _U^* \mathcal{F}\), which is identified with \(\iota _{V'}^* (g'^* \mathcal{F})\) by pseudofunctoriality of pullback along \(\iota _U \circ h = g' \circ \iota _{V'}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_pullback_mathlib">1097</a>). Reading off global sections over \(V'\) — the identification \(\Gamma (\iota _{V'}^* g'^* \mathcal{F}, V') = \Gamma (g'^* \mathcal{F}, V')\) is equivariant for the ring identification \(\mathcal{O}_{V'}(V') = \mathcal{O}_{X'}(V')\), which carries \(h^\sharp r_0\) to the image of \(r\) — the image of \(r\) annihilates \(\Gamma (g'^* \mathcal{F}, V')\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:10594:  <p>[The annihilator ideal sheaf pulls back]    stacks-project <i class="itshape">Source: Stacks <a href ="https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/056H">056H</a>.</i> Let \(g' : X' \to X\) be a morphism of schemes and \(\mathcal{F}\) a finitely presented sheaf of \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-modules. Write \(\iota ' : Z' \to X'\) for the schematic-support immersion of \(g'^* \mathcal{F}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:schematic_support_immersion">1122</a>). Then \(\mathrm{Ann}(\mathcal{F})\) is contained in the kernel ideal sheaf of \(\mathcal{O}_X \to (\iota ' \circ g')_* \mathcal{O}_{Z'}\); equivalently, \(g' \circ \iota '\) factors through the schematic support \(Z \subseteq X\) of \(\mathcal{F}\) by a morphism \(l : Z' \to Z\) over \(g'\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:10606:  <p> The kernel ideal sheaf of \((\iota ' \circ g')^\sharp \) is the largest ideal sheaf whose value on each affine open \(U \subseteq X\) is contained in \(\ker \bigl((\iota ' \circ g')^\sharp _U\bigr)\), so it suffices to prove, for each affine open \(U\) and each \(r \in \mathrm{Ann}(\mathcal{F})(U)\), that \((\iota ' \circ g')^\sharp _U(r) = 0\) in \(\Gamma \bigl(Z', (\iota ' \circ g')^{-1}(U)\bigr)\). By <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_annihilator_ideal_le">1091</a>, \(r\) annihilates \(\Gamma (\mathcal{F}, U)\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:10607:<p>The open \((\iota ')^{-1}(g'^{-1}(U))\) of \(Z'\) is covered by the preimages \((\iota ')^{-1}(V')\) of the affine opens \(V' \subseteq g'^{-1}(U)\) of \(X'\), and the structure sheaf of \(Z'\) is separated, so it suffices that the restriction of \((\iota ' \circ g')^\sharp _U(r)\) to each \((\iota ')^{-1}(V')\) vanishes. By naturality of \(\iota '^\sharp \), that restriction is \(\iota '^\sharp _{V'}(\rho )\), where \(\rho \in \mathcal{O}_{X'}(V')\) is the image of \(r\). By <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:annihilator_pullback_sections">1131</a>, \(\rho \) annihilates \(\Gamma (g'^* \mathcal{F}, V')\). The pullback \(g'^* \mathcal{F}\) is finitely presented (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:pullback_finite_presentation">1127</a>), hence quasi-coherent with finite section modules on all affine opens (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:finite_sections_affine_all">1130</a>); therefore \(\mathrm{Ann}_{\mathcal{O}_{X'}(V')}\Gamma (g'^* \mathcal{F}, V') = \mathrm{Ann}(g'^* \mathcal{F})(V')\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_annihilator_ideal">1092</a>), and on affine opens the subscheme immersion of an ideal sheaf kills exactly that ideal, so \(\iota '^\sharp _{V'}(\rho ) = 0\), as required. Finally, a morphism to \(X\) under whose structure map the defining ideal sheaf of the closed subscheme \(Z\) dies factors through \(Z\); this produces \(l : Z' \to Z\) with \(\iota \circ l = g' \circ \iota '\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:10681:  <p>[Proper support is stable under base change]    nitsure-hilbert-quot <i class="itshape">Source: [Nitsure], §1 (FGA Explained Ch. 5); Stacks 01W4, 056H.</i> In the cartesian square of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:coherent_flat_base_change">1128</a>, let \(\mathcal{F}\) be a finitely presented sheaf of \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-modules whose schematic support is proper over \(S\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:has_proper_support">1124</a>). Then the schematic support of \(g'^* \mathcal{F}\) is proper over \(S'\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:10693:  <p> Write \(\iota : Z \to X\) and \(\iota ' : Z' \to X'\) for the schematic-support immersions (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:schematic_support_immersion">1122</a>) of \(\mathcal{F}\) and of \(g'^* \mathcal{F}\). By <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:annihilator_le_map_pullback">1132</a> there is a morphism \(l : Z' \to Z\) with \(\iota \circ l = g' \circ \iota '\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:10694:<p>Form the fibre product \(W := Z \times _X X'\) with projections \(p : W \to Z\) and \(q : W \to X'\). Pasting its defining cartesian square vertically with the given cartesian square exhibits \(W\), together with \(p\) and \(f' \circ q\), as the fibre product of \(Z \xrightarrow {\, f \circ \iota \, } S \xleftarrow {\, g\, } S'\). The hypothesis says \(f \circ \iota \) is proper, and properness is stable under base change (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isProper_mathlib">1123</a>), so \(f' \circ q : W \to S'\) is proper. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:10695:<p>The pair \((l, \iota ')\) induces \(c : Z' \to W\) with \(q \circ c = \iota '\). The immersion \(\iota '\) is a closed immersion, hence proper; and \(q\) is a closed immersion (the base change of the closed immersion \(\iota \) along \(g'\)), hence separated. By cancellation of properness along separated morphisms applied to \(q \circ c = \iota '\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isProper_mathlib">1123</a>), \(c\) is proper. Finally </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html:10699:<p> is a composite of proper morphisms, hence proper (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isProper_mathlib">1123</a>); that is, the schematic support of \(g'^* \mathcal{F}\) is proper over \(S'\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:1715:<p>Throughout this chapter, fix a base field \(k\) and a smooth proper geometrically integral curve \(C\) over \(k\) (the curve carrying the Jacobian). The relative Picard presheaf \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k} : (\operatorname{Sch}/k)^{op} \to \mathrm{Set}\) of <a href="chap-Picard_LineBundlePullback.html">14</a> has already been packaged as a set-valued functor and refined to its abelian-group-valued étale-sheafified version \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\) in <a href="chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html">15</a>. The Quot scheme machinery of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html">20</a> supplies the representing engine: for \(C/k\) projective and flat with integral geometric fibers, the Hilbert scheme \(\operatorname {Hilb}_{C/k}\) and its open subscheme \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) of relative effective divisors are both representable by quasi-projective \(k\)-schemes. Grothendieck’s existence theorem for \(\operatorname{Pic}\) assembles these two ingredients via the Abel map \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) to produce a representing scheme, the <em>Picard scheme</em> \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\). The present chapter packages this assembly: a line-bundle / Quot correspondence, the FGA representability theorem, and the abelian-group-scheme refinement. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:1717:<p><b class="bfseries">Comparison with the sheafified Picard functor.</b> Kleiman §4 represents the étale-sheafified functor \(\operatorname{Pic}_{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\). This chapter instead works throughout under the standing hypothesis that <em>\(C\) has a \(k\)-rational point</em> (<a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:has_rational_point">1537</a>) and states representability against the <em>plain</em> relative Picard functor \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) of <a href="chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html#def:rel_pic_sharp">621</a>. This is justified by Kleiman §2, Thm. 2.5 (<span class="ttfamily">th:comp</span>): if \(f : X \to S\) has a section and \(\mathcal O_{S'} = f'_* \mathcal O_{X'}\) holds for all base changes (automatic for our proper geometrically integral curve, by cohomology and base change), then the comparison maps </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:1724:<p>The bridge from line bundles on \(C \times _k T\) to the Quot scheme is the Abel map: a relative effective divisor \(D \subset C \times _k T\) over \(T\) (a \(T\)-flat closed subscheme whose ideal is invertible) determines a closed subscheme of \(C \times _k T\) flat over \(T\), hence a \(T\)-point of the Hilbert functor \(\operatorname {Hilb}_{C/k}(T)\), which is the special case \(\operatorname {Quot}_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) of the Quot functor of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html">20</a>; and it determines an invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_{C \times _k T}(D)\) on the relative curve, representing a class in \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}(T)\). </p>

There is a natural transformation of presheaves on \((\operatorname{Sch}/k)^{op}\) </p>

This transformation is the required witness for \(\mathrm{HasAbelMap}(C)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:has_abel_map">1542</a>). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:1920:  <p>  Kleiman §3, Thm. th:repDiv, shows that \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) is representable by an open subscheme \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \subseteq \operatorname {Hilb}_{C/k}\) of the Hilbert scheme (\(\operatorname {Hilb}_{C/k} = \operatorname {Quot}_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\), <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html">20</a>): letting \(W \subseteq C \times _k \operatorname {Hilb}_{C/k}\) be the universal closed subscheme and \(q \colon W \to \operatorname {Hilb}_{C/k}\) the projection, the locus \(V \subseteq W\) where \(W\) is locally an effective Cartier divisor is open, so \(Z := q(W \setminus V)\) is closed (\(q\) proper) and \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} := \operatorname {Hilb}_{C/k} \setminus Z\) is the open subscheme representing relative effective divisors. This is the relative-divisor functor appearing in <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:div_functor_carrier">1540</a>. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:1926:<p>We now state and prove the specialisation of Grothendieck’s existence theorem for the Picard scheme, in the specialisation needed for the Jacobian: \(S = \operatorname{Spec}k\), \(X = C\) a smooth proper geometrically integral curve. The general theorem (Kleiman §4, Thm. 4.8) covers any \(X/S\) projective Zariski-locally over \(S\), flat, with integral geometric fibers; we record the general statement and then specialise. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:1960:          <li><a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#thm:quot_representable">Theorem 1217</a></li>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:2003:  <p>[FGA representability of the Picard scheme]    <i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §4, Main Thm. 4.8 + Cor. 4.18.3.</i> Let \(k\) be a field and \(C\) a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over \(k\) <em>with a \(k\)-rational point</em> (<a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:has_rational_point">1537</a>). Then the relative Picard functor \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) of <a href="chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html#def:rel_pic_sharp">621</a> — which under the rational-point hypothesis coincides with its étale sheafification \(\operatorname{Pic}_{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\), by Kleiman §2, Thm. 2.5 — is representable by a \(k\)-scheme \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\), separated and locally of finite type over \(k\), which is a disjoint union of open quasi-projective \(k\)-subschemes, each an increasing union of open quasi-projective subschemes. The scheme \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) is called the <em>Picard scheme</em> of \(C/k\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:2015:  <p>We follow Kleiman §4, Thm. 4.8, specialised to \(S = \operatorname{Spec}k\) and \(X = C\). The proof proceeds in four conceptual steps, preceded by a comparison step; the underlying algebraic engine is the Quot scheme of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html">20</a> and the relative Picard functor of <a href="chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html">15</a>, together with the line-bundle / Quot correspondence of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence">1531</a>. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:2016:<p><em>Step 0: reduce to the étale sheaf via the rational point.</em> By Kleiman §2, Thm. 2.5, since \(C \to \operatorname{Spec}k\) has a section (<a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:has_rational_point">1537</a>) and \(\mathcal O_T = \pi _{T*} \mathcal O_{C \times _k T}\) holds for every \(k\)-scheme \(T\) (cohomology and base change for the proper geometrically integral fibers of \(C\times _k T/T\)), the comparison map \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}(T) \to \operatorname{Pic}_{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(T)\) is bijective for all \(T\). It therefore suffices to represent the étale sheaf \(\operatorname{Pic}_{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\), which is what Kleiman’s theorem produces; the same scheme then represents \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:2017:<p><em>Step 1: stratify by Hilbert polynomial.</em> For each polynomial \(\phi \in \mathbb {Q}[n]\), let \(P^\phi \subseteq \operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\) be the étale subsheaf whose \(T\)-points are represented by invertible sheaves \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C \times _k T\) with \(\chi (C_t, \mathcal{L}_t^{-1}(n)) = \phi (n)\) for all \(t \in T\) (the Hilbert polynomial relative to the chosen polarisation \(\mathcal{O}_C(1)\) on the projective curve \(C\)). The \(P^\phi \) form a disjoint open cover of \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\) (openness via Kleiman’s flat-base-change argument, <a href="chap-Cohomology_CechHigherDirectImage.html#lem:cech_flat_base_change">480</a> / Stacks Tag 02KH; cf. EGA III 7.9.11). It suffices to represent each \(P^\phi \) by an increasing union of open quasi-projective \(k\)-schemes. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:2019:<p><em>Step 3: factor through the Abel map.</em> Consider the Abel map \(A_{C/k} : \mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\) of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence">1531</a>. The source \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) is representable by an open subscheme of \(\operatorname {Hilb}_{C/k}\) (and hence by an open subscheme of the Quot scheme of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#thm:quot_representable">1217</a>), and is quasi-projective over \(k\). Pulling back along \(P^{\phi _0}_0 \hookrightarrow \operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\) yields an open subscheme \(Z := P^{\phi _0}_0 \times _{\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}} \mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) of \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\), which is again quasi-projective. The projection \(\alpha : Z \to P^{\phi _0}_0\) is a surjection of étale sheaves: given a \(T\)-point \(\lambda \) of \(P^{\phi _0}_0\) represented by an étale cover \(T' \to T\) and an invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{L}'\) on \(C \times _k T'\) with \(H^1(C_{t'}, \mathcal{L}'_{t'}) = 0\), the projective bundle \(\mathbb {P}(\mathcal{Q}) \to T'\) associated to \(\mathcal{Q} := \pi _{T'*}\mathcal{L}'\) is smooth over \(T'\); an étale cover \(T_1 \to T'\) admits a \(T'\)-map \(T_1 \to \mathbb {P}(\mathcal{Q})\) (EGA IV 17.16.3 (ii)) whose composition with the universal divisor map \(\mathbb {P}(\mathcal{Q}) \to Z\) produces the required \(T_1\)-point of \(Z\). Moreover, the first projection \(Z \times _{P^{\phi _0}_0} Z \to Z\) is smooth and proper. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:2020:<p><em>Step 4: descend by the smooth-proper quotient lemma.</em> Apply Kleiman §4, Lem. 4.9: given a surjection \(\alpha : Z \to P\) of étale sheaves with \(Z\) quasi-projective, \(R := Z \times _P Z\) representable, and the first projection \(R \to Z\) smooth and proper, \(P\) is representable by a quasi-projective scheme. In our case \(P = P^{\phi _0}_0\), \(Z\) and \(R\) as above, so \(P^{\phi _0}_0\) is quasi-projective. Reassembling over \(\phi \in \mathbb {Q}[n]\) and over \(m\), the disjoint union of representable \(P^\phi \) pieces represents \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\). The total scheme is separated (as a disjoint union of separated quasi-projectives) and locally of finite type. This is Kleiman §4, Cor. 4.18.3 in the \(S = \operatorname{Spec}k\), \(X = C\) complete case. </p>

Set \(R := Z \times _P Z\). Suppose: </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:2111:<p>Hence \(R \hookrightarrow Z \times _k Z\) is a flat (by (iv)) and proper equivalence relation on the quasi-projective \(k\)-scheme \(Z\). By the theory of flat-and-proper effective equivalence relations on quasi-projective schemes (Altman–Kleiman; the construction places the graph \(R \subseteq Z \times _k Z\) inside the universal subscheme of the Hilbert scheme \(\operatorname {Hilb}_{Z/k}\) and descends to a closed subscheme \(Q \subseteq \operatorname {Hilb}_{Z/k}\) representing the quotient), there exist a quasi-projective \(k\)-scheme \(Q\) and a faithfully flat, projective map \(Z \to Q\) with \(R = Z \times _Q Z\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:2189:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §2, Def. 2.2 + §4, Def. 4.1 (the Picard scheme).</i> Let \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) be the Picard scheme of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#thm:fga_pic_representability">1533</a>. Then \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) is canonically an abelian group scheme over \(k\): the tensor product \([\mathcal{L}] + [\mathcal{M}] := [\mathcal{L} \otimes \mathcal{M}]\) and inverse \(-[\mathcal{L}] := [\mathcal{L}^{-1}]\) on \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}(T)\) (well defined because both operations preserve isomorphism classes and descend through the subgroup \(H_T = \pi _T^*\operatorname{Pic}(T)\) of <a href="chap-Picard_LineBundlePullback.html#thm:relative_pic_quotient_well_defined">604</a>) are natural in \(T\), hence by Yoneda are represented by morphisms \(m : \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k} \times _k \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k} \to \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\), \(i : \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k} \to \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\), and \(e : \operatorname{Spec}k \to \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) (the trivial line bundle class) satisfying the abelian-group axioms. In particular, \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) is a \(k\)-group scheme locally of finite type. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:2271:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §4, Def. 4.1.</i> Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field \(k\), with a \(k\)-rational point. The <em>Picard scheme</em> \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) is the \(k\)-scheme representing the relative Picard functor \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) (equivalently, by Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 under the rational point, its étale sheafification), supplied by <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#thm:fga_pic_representability">1533</a>, equipped with the abelian-group-scheme structure of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#thm:pic_is_group_scheme">1535</a>. The scheme is separated, locally of finite type over \(k\), and a disjoint union of open quasi-projective \(k\)-subschemes. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:2289:  <li><p>The Altman–Kleiman lemma <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#lem:smooth_proper_quotient">1534</a> gives descent of a flat-and-proper equivalence relation \(R \subseteq Z \times _k Z\) on a quasi-projective \(k\)-scheme \(Z\) to a quasi-projective quotient \(Q\) representing the coequalising sheaf. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:2344:  <p>[\(k\)-rational point]   The predicate \(\mathrm{HasRationalPoint}(C)\) asserts that the structural morphism \(C \to \operatorname{Spec}k\) admits a section \(\sigma : \operatorname{Spec}k \to C\), i.e. that \(C\) has a \(k\)-rational point. This is the standing hypothesis of the chapter (see <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#sec:fga_pic_setup">25.1</a>): by Kleiman §2, Thm. 2.5, it makes the plain relative Picard functor \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) coincide with its étale (and fppf) sheafification, so representability can be stated against <a href="chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html#def:rel_pic_sharp">621</a> directly. For a pointed curve \((C,P)\), the pointing \(P\) supplies this section. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:2870:  <p>[Representability of the smooth-proper quotient]   For a morphism \(\alpha : Z \to P\) of presheaves of types on \((\operatorname{Sch}/k)^{op}\), the predicate \(\mathrm{HasSmoothProperQuotient}(\alpha )\) asserts that the target \(P\) is representable. It records the conclusion of the Altman–Kleiman lemma <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#lem:smooth_proper_quotient">1534</a> for the quotient occurring in the FGA construction. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:2948:  <p>[Existence of the Picard scheme]    The predicate \(\mathrm{HasPicScheme}(C)\) asserts that there exists a \(k\)-scheme \(X\), <em>locally of finite type over \(k\)</em>, carrying a representability witness for the relative Picard functor \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:pic_sharp_carrier">1538</a>; in other words, that the Picard scheme \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) exists and is locally of finite type. It is the existence assertion from which <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:pic_scheme">1536</a> extracts the representing object. The local-finiteness clause belongs to the same existence package as representability: Kleiman §4, Thm. th:main exhibits \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) as a disjoint union of open quasi-projective \(k\)-subschemes. The witness <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:inst_has_pic_scheme">1546</a> is conditional on the \(k\)-rational point of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:has_rational_point">1537</a>. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:3270:<p> asserts that the structural morphism of the Picard scheme \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:pic_scheme">1536</a> is locally of finite type — part (1) of Kleiman §4, Thm. th:main (\(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) is a disjoint union of open quasi-projective \(k\)-subschemes). It is the hypothesis the identity-component construction of <a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html">26</a> uses to specialise \(G^0\) to \(G = \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\). It follows from the local-finiteness component of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:has_pic_scheme">1545</a>. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:3352:  <p>[Local-finiteness assertion]    Whenever <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:has_pic_scheme">1545</a> holds, the second component of its chosen witness gives local finiteness of \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\). Thus representability and local finiteness are supplied by one existence package, as in Kleiman §4, Thm. th:main. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:3373:<p>For a smooth proper geometrically integral curve \(C/k\) with a \(k\)-rational point, the relative Picard functor \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:pic_sharp_carrier">1538</a>) is representable by a \(k\)-scheme. The proof first applies Kleiman §2, Thm. 2.5, using the section to identify the plain functor with its étale sheafification, and then uses Kleiman’s four steps (<a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#thm:fga_pic_representability">1533</a>): Hilbert-polynomial stratification, \(m\)-regularity bound, Abel-map factorisation through \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\), and the smooth-proper quotient (<a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#lem:smooth_proper_quotient">1534</a>). Its inputs are the Quot/Hilbert construction of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html">20</a>, representability of \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) as in <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#rem:div_functor_representability">1532</a>, the regularity result <a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#cor:flattening_stratification_curve">1005</a>, the base-change result <a href="chap-Cohomology_CechHigherDirectImage.html#lem:cech_flat_base_change">480</a>, and Altman–Kleiman effective descent. The resulting representing object gives natural bijections </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html:3380:<p>The relative-divisor functor \(\operatorname{Div}_{X/S}\) of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:div_functor">1163</a> is the subfunctor of the Hilbert functor \(\operatorname {Hilb}_{C/k} = \operatorname {Quot}_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) of relative effective Cartier divisors, in the invertible-kernel quotient encoding of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:div_family">1147</a>. The presheaf \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:div_functor_carrier">1540</a> is its instantiation at \(C\to \operatorname{Spec}k\). Its divisor condition is stable under base change by <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:relative_divisor_base_change">1153</a>, while representability of \(\operatorname{Div}_{C/k}\) by an open subscheme of the Hilbert scheme (Kleiman §3, Thm. th:repDiv) is the content of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#rem:div_functor_representability">1532</a>. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:3524:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §5, Thm. 5.11; cf. [Hartshorne], “Algebraic Geometry”, GTM 52, IV.1.1 (genus def. \(g(C) = \dim _k H^1(C, \mathcal{O}_C)\)).</i> Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve of genus \(g = g(C)\) over a field \(k\), and let \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#def:pic_zero_subscheme">1576</a>) be the identity component of the Picard scheme of \(C/k\). There is a canonical isomorphism of \(k\)-vector spaces </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:3540:  <p> We follow Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.11. By <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#thm:fga_pic_representability">1533</a>, the Picard scheme \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) exists and represents the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor \(\operatorname{Pic}_{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\); the identity component \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) is an open subscheme of \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#thm:identity_component_open_subgroup">1552</a>), so the tangent spaces at the identity of \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) and of \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) agree; we may therefore work with \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) throughout. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:3558:<p> whose vertical maps are isomorphisms after base change to the algebraic closure \(\bar k\) (Kleiman §2, Exercise 2.3; invocation legitimised by <a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#thm:identity_component_base_change_commutes">1555</a>). Taking horizontal kernels yields a \(k\)-linear comparison map \(v : H^1(C, \mathcal{O}_C) \to \textup T_0 \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) which is an isomorphism after base change to \(\bar k\), hence already an isomorphism over \(k\) (the source and target are finite-dimensional \(k\)-vector spaces, and an isomorphism of \(k\)-vector spaces is detected after a faithfully flat extension). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:4718:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §5, Cor. 5.13 + Cor. 5.14; cf. [Milne], “Abelian Varieties” (course notes, 2008), §III.1, Rmk. 1.4(e), p. 86 (dimension of \(J\) equals the genus).</i> Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve of genus \(g\) over a field \(k\). The identity component \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#def:pic_zero_subscheme">1576</a>) is smooth over \(k\) of dimension \(g\): the structural morphism \((\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}) \to \operatorname{Spec}k\) is smooth, and every closed point of \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) lies in a smooth open neighbourhood. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:4730:  <p> We follow Kleiman §5 Cor. 5.13, with the curve-specific dimension input supplied by <a href="chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html#thm:pic0_tangent_space_iso">1604</a>. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:4733:<p>It remains to show that for \(C/k\) a smooth proper curve, equality holds (so smoothness of \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) follows). For a smooth proper curve there is no obstruction: as Kleiman §5 Ex. 5.23 notes, projectivity and flatness of \(C/k\) together with the smoothness of \(C\) over \(k\) imply that \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) is a smooth quasi-projective family of relative dimension \(p_a(C) = g(C)\). In characteristic zero this reduces to Cartier’s theorem (Kleiman §5 Cor. 5.14): every \(k\)-group scheme locally of finite type over a field of characteristic zero is smooth; in positive characteristic the smoothness uses the curve-specific Hodge-theoretic vanishing \(H^2(C, \mathcal{O}_C) = 0\) (the source-target of the obstruction to lifting tangent vectors to first-order deformations), which holds for any curve since \(C\) has dimension \(1\). In either case \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) is smooth at \(0\); by the translation argument above, it is smooth everywhere. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:4740:<p>A smooth proper geometrically integral curve is geometrically normal, so Kleiman’s \(\operatorname{Pic}^0\)-projectivity theorem applies and upgrades the quasi-projective conclusion to projective: \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) is projective over \(k\), in particular proper. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:4810:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §5, Thm. 5.4; cf. [Milne], “Abelian Varieties” (course notes, 2008), §I.6 (abelian varieties are projective, p. 27).</i> Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field \(k\). The identity component \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#def:pic_zero_subscheme">1576</a>) is projective over \(k\), in particular proper: the structural morphism \((\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}) \to \operatorname{Spec}k\) is a projective morphism, hence satisfies the universal closedness and separatedness conditions of properness. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:4822:  <p> We follow Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.4, specialised to \(X = C\) a smooth proper geometrically integral curve. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:4823:<p><em>Quasi-projectivity.</em> By <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#thm:fga_pic_representability">1533</a>, \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) exists, represents \(\operatorname{Pic}_{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\), and is locally of finite type; its identity component \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) is of finite type by <a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#thm:identity_component_finite_type_geom_irreducible">1554</a>. Kleiman’s quasi-projectivity statement (§5 Thm. 5.4, first conclusion) then gives that \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) is a quasi-projective \(k\)-scheme, since \(C/k\) is projective and geometrically integral. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:4826:<p><em>No non-constant map from \(\mathbb {G}_m\) (uses geometric normality of \(C\)).</em> The smooth proper curve \(C/\bar k\) is in particular geometrically normal. Suppose \(t : T \to \operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/\bar k}\), where \(T = \mathbb {A}^1 \setminus \{ 0\} \) is the multiplicative group; by the comparison theorem (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5) \(t\) is represented by an invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C \times T\). Since \(C \times T\) is normal and integral, every invertible sheaf is the sheaf of a Cartier divisor: write \(\mathcal{L} = \mathcal{O}_{C \times T}(D)\) for some divisor \(D\) (Hartshorne II Ex. 6.15). Restricting \(\mathcal{L}\) to the generic fibre of the projection \(p : C \times T \to C\): the generic fibre is \(T\) localised at the generic point of \(C\), and an invertible sheaf on an open subscheme of \(\mathbb {A}^1\) is trivial. Hence there is a rational function \(\phi \) on \(C \times T\) such that \((\phi ) + D\) restricts to the trivial divisor on the generic fibre. Pick any section \(s : C \to C \times T\) of \(p\) (e.g. at a closed point of \(T\)), and set \(E := s^*((\phi ) + D)\); then \(E\) is a divisor on \(C\) with the property that \(p^* E\) and \((\phi ) + D\) coincide as cycles, hence as divisors (Altman–Kleiman AK70, Prp. 3.10, p. 139, valid since \(C \times T\) is normal). Therefore \(\mathcal{L} \cong p^* \mathcal{O}_C(E)\), so the associated map \(t : T \to \operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/\bar k}\) factors through the generic fibre and is constant. This rules out non-constant maps \(\mathbb {G}_m \to \operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\); the additive case \(\mathbb {G}_a \to \operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) is analogous (and follows from the multiplicative case via the standard embedding \(\mathbb {G}_a \hookrightarrow \mathbb {G}_m\) on solvable subgroups). Hence the linear part in the Chevalley–Rosenlicht decomposition of \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) is trivial, so \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) is an abelian variety; in particular, it is proper. Combined with quasi-projectivity, this yields projectivity of \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) over \(\bar k\), hence over \(k\) by faithfully flat descent of properness. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:4904:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §5, Prp. 5.3 (geometric irreducibility of the connected component of the identity).</i> Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field \(k\). The identity component \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#def:pic_zero_subscheme">1576</a>) is geometrically irreducible: after base change to the algebraic closure \(\bar k\), the scheme \((\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k})_{\bar k}\) is irreducible. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:5002:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Milne], “Abelian Varieties” (course notes, 2008), §I.1, p. 8 (definition of abelian variety); [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §5, Rmk. 5.26 (the Jacobian \(J := \operatorname{Pic}^0_{X/S}\) of a smooth proper family of curves is a projective abelian \(S\)-scheme).</i> Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve of genus \(g\) over a field \(k\). The identity component \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#def:pic_zero_subscheme">1576</a>) is an <em>abelian variety over \(k\)</em> of dimension \(g\): the underlying \(k\)-scheme is smooth (<a href="chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html#thm:pic0_smooth">1620</a>), proper (<a href="chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html#thm:pic0_proper">1621</a>), and geometrically irreducible (<a href="chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html#thm:pic0_geom_irred">1622</a>), and it carries a \(k\)-group-scheme structure inherited from \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) via the inclusion \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k} \hookrightarrow \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#thm:identity_component_is_subgroup_homomorphism">1553</a>). In particular, \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) is automatically commutative (Milne §I.1, Cor. 1.4). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:5020:<p>This is the content of Kleiman §5 Rmk. 5.26: for \(X/S\) projective and smooth with connected curve fibres of genus \(g {\gt} 0\) (specialise to \(S = \operatorname{Spec}k\), \(X = C\)), the Jacobian \(J := \operatorname{Pic}^0_{X/S}\) exists and is a projective abelian \(S\)-scheme. The genus-zero case is degenerate (\(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k} = 0\), Milne §III.1, Rmk. 1.4(e)) but is consistent with the assembly: a point scheme \(\operatorname{Spec}k\) is trivially an abelian variety of dimension \(0\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:5028:  <li><p><span class="ttfamily">AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.tangentSpaceIso</span> (<a href="chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html#thm:pic0_tangent_space_iso">1604</a>) packages the canonical isomorphism \(\textup T_0 \operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k} \cong H^1(C, \mathcal{O}_C)\), the curve-specific content of Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.11. In Lean this is an isomorphism of \(k\)-modules between the Zariski tangent space of \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) at the identity \(0\) and the first sheaf-cohomology \(k\)-module \(H^1(C, \mathcal{O}_C)\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html:5030:  <li><p><span class="ttfamily">AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.smooth</span> (<a href="chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html#thm:pic0_smooth">1620</a>) packages the smoothness of \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) as a <span class="ttfamily">[Smooth]</span> instance on the structural morphism, of relative dimension \(g\). Kleiman §5 Cor. 5.13 + Cor. 5.14. </p>

Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.4 (projectivity upgrade for geometrically normal \(C/k\)). </p>

Then the Hilbert polynomial of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:hilbert_polynomial">1006</a> is the polynomial extracted from the pair \((p, d)\) by <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:hilbertPoly_exists_mathlib">1013</a>: \(\Phi _{\mathcal{F},s} = \mathrm{hilbertPoly}\, p\, d\). </p>

If <em>some</em> polynomial in \(\mathbb {Q}[\lambda ]\) agrees with \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) at all sufficiently large integers, then the Hilbert polynomial \(\Phi _{\mathcal{F},s}\) of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:hilbert_polynomial">1006</a> does: \(\Phi _{\mathcal{F},s}(m) = h_{\mathcal{F},s}(m)\) for all \(m \gg 0\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:510:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>    Every member of the Serre twist family — the twist on the glued model, on the integral model \(\operatorname {Proj}\mathbb {Z}[X_i]\), and on the relative projective space \(\mathbb {P}(n; S)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:serreTwist_isLocallyTrivial">1183</a>: each is locally trivial) — is invertible in the sense of <a href="chap-Picard_SectionGradedRing.html#def:isInvertible">1269</a>. Consequently <a href="chap-Picard_SectionGradedRing.html#lem:sectionGradedRing_gcommSemiring">1329</a> applies unconditionally to each: its section ring \(\bigoplus _{m \ge 0} \Gamma (-, \mathcal{O}(m))\) is graded-commutative. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:877:<p> on the iso-class carrier, with the tensor-product group law of <a href="chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html#lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid">606</a> and the pullback structure maps of <a href="chap-Picard_LineBundlePullback.html#thm:pullback_natural">605</a>. In Kleiman’s notation this is \(\operatorname{Pic}_X\) of df:aPf (with \(X = C \times _k -\) over the test scheme). The Lean declaration bundles the object/morphism data directly; the helpers <span class="ttfamily">PicSharp.functorial</span> (group-hom form of the structure maps) and <span class="ttfamily">PicSharp.presheaf</span> (a re-export of the bundle) belong to this node. It compares onto the relative functor of <a href="chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html#def:rel_pic_sharp">621</a> via <a href="chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html#lem:relpic_quotient_comparison">626</a>. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:2919:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Family of relative effective divisors]    kleiman-picard <i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], §3, Defs. df:red and df:div (FGA Explained Ch. 9).</i> Let \(\pi : X \to S\) be a morphism of schemes and \(T \to S\) an \(S\)-scheme; write \(X_T := X \times _S T\). A <em>family of relative effective divisors on \(X_T/T\)</em> is a pair \((\mathcal F, q)\) where </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:2921:  <li><p>\(\mathcal F\) is a finitely presented sheaf of \(\mathcal O_{X_T}\)-modules, flat over \(T\) (<a href="chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html#def:coherent_sheaf_flat">909</a>) and with schematic support proper over \(T\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:has_proper_support">1124</a>); </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:2929:<p>Such a pair is precisely the structure-sheaf quotient \(q : \mathcal O_{X_T} \to \mathcal O_D\) of a relative effective divisor \(D \subseteq X_T\) in the sense of [Kleiman] df:red — a closed subscheme, flat over \(T\), whose ideal is invertible — subject to two conditions that are automatic in the regime of interest: finite presentation of \(\mathcal O_D\) always holds (\(\mathcal O_D\) is the cokernel of \(\mathcal I \hookrightarrow \mathcal O_{X_T}\) with \(\mathcal I\) locally free of rank one), and properness of the support \(D\) over \(T\) holds whenever \(\pi \) is proper (a closed subscheme of the \(T\)-proper \(X_T\) is proper over \(T\)). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:2932:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:div_family">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:2959:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Relative-divisor functor]    kleiman-picard <i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], §3, Def. df:div (FGA Explained Ch. 9).</i> Let \(\pi : X \to S\) be a morphism of schemes. The <em>relative-divisor functor</em> </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:2963:<p> sends an \(S\)-scheme \(T \to S\) to the set of equivalence classes of families of relative effective divisors on \(X_T/T\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:div_family">1147</a>) — equivalently, the set of relative effective divisors on \(X_T/T\) — and an \(S\)-morphism \(T' \to T\) to the pullback of families along the induced morphism \(g' : X_{T'} \to X_T\). The action is well defined: pullback of modules preserves surjectivity (it is right exact), finite presentation (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:pullback_finite_presentation">1127</a>), flatness over the base (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:coherent_flat_base_change">1128</a>) and proper support (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:proper_support_base_change">1133</a>), and it preserves the invertibility of the kernel ideal because the pulled-back kernel is the kernel of the pulled-back quotient (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:relative_divisor_base_change">1153</a>, applicable since the source of \(q\) is always a pullback of the unit module \(\mathcal O_X\), quasi-coherent by <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:unit_isQuasicoherent">1162</a> together with pullback-stability of quasi-coherence (<a href="chap-Cohomology_CechHigherDirectImage.html#lem:pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom">507</a>)). Functoriality holds because the pullback of modules is pseudofunctorial in the scheme morphism. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:2966:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:div_functor">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:2993:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[The relative-divisor functor]    The presheaf \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} : (\operatorname{Sch}/k)^{op} \to \mathrm{Set}\) is the relative-divisor functor \(\operatorname{Div}_{C/k}\) of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:div_functor">1163</a>, instantiated at the structural morphism \(C \to \operatorname{Spec}k\): it sends a \(k\)-scheme \(T\) to the set of relative effective Cartier divisors on \(C \times _k T\) flat over \(T\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:3130:<p> is defined as follows: a \(k\)-point \(\lambda \in \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(k)\) represents (after étale base change) an invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C\); its Hilbert polynomial with respect to a fixed degree-one polarisation \(\mathcal{O}_C(1)\) on \(C\) is, by <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:hilbert_polynomial">1006</a> and Riemann–Roch, </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:3540:<p> where \(\mathcal{F}_s\) and \(L_s\) are the restrictions to the fibre \(X_s\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:fiber_module_restriction">1007</a>), the twist \(\mathcal{F}_s \otimes L_s^{\otimes m}\) is the \(m\)-twist of \(\mathcal{F}_s\) by \(L_s\) on \(X_s\) (<a href="chap-Picard_SectionGradedRing.html#def:sheafModuleTwist">1270</a>), and the dimension is taken with respect to the \(\kappa (s)\)-vector-space structure on sections over the fibre (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:fiber_sections_module">1008</a>). This is exactly the graded Hilbert function of the section graded module \(M(X_s, \mathcal{F}_s, L_s)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:sectionGradedModule">1010</a>); it uses only global sections \(H^0\). </p>

The fibre \(X_s = X \times _S \operatorname{Spec}\kappa (s)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:fiber_module_restriction">1007</a>) carries a structural morphism \(p_s : X_s \to \operatorname{Spec}\kappa (s)\), the second projection of the fibre product. Taking global sections of \(p_s\) and identifying \(\Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}\kappa (s), \mathcal{O}) = \kappa (s)\) yields the <em>structural ring homomorphism of the fibre</em> </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:4613:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Overlap base change in pullback form]    Conjugating the overlap base change \(\beta _{ij}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_GlueDescent.html#lem:glueOverlapBaseChangeIso">1435</a>) on both sides by the comparison <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_mathlib">1099</a> between the site-level restriction and the geometric pullback yields the isomorphism, in geometric form, </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:5303:<p> sends each variable \(X_i\) to \(t_i\). It is constructed by evaluating into the <em>commutative</em> \(\kappa \)-subalgebra \(A = \mathrm{adjoin}_\kappa (\{ t_i\} ) \subseteq \operatorname {End}_\kappa (M)\) – commutative by <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:adjoinCommRingOfComm_mathlib">1037</a> because the generators commute – and then including \(A \hookrightarrow \operatorname {End}_\kappa (M)\); evaluation into the noncommutative \(\operatorname {End}_\kappa (M)\) directly is not an algebra homomorphism, which is why the commutative \(A\) is interposed. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:5306:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyEndHom">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:5333:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Polynomial-ring module structure on \(M\)]    The <em>polynomial-module structure</em> is the \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\)-module structure on \(M\) obtained by restricting scalars along \(\mathrm{polyEndHom}(t)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyEndHom">1068</a>): a polynomial \(p\) acts on \(m \in M\) by \(p \cdot m = \mathrm{polyEndHom}(t)(p)(m)\). This is the module over the free polynomial ring on which the ambient subquotient induction’s finiteness condition is measured. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:5336:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyModule">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:5363:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Polynomial-ring submodule from a \(t\)-stable submodule]    Let \(N \subseteq M\) be a \(\kappa \)-submodule that is stable under each \(t_i\) (\(t_i \cdot N \subseteq N\)). Then \(N\), with the <em>same</em> ambient carrier, is a \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\)-submodule of \(M\) for the polynomial-module structure (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyModule">1071</a>). Stability under the action of an arbitrary polynomial follows by induction on monomials: constants act as scalars (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyModule_C_smul">1073</a>) and multiplication by \(X_i\) acts as \(t_i\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyModule_X_smul">1072</a>), both of which preserve \(N\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:5366:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polySubmodule">LaTeX</a>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:5427:<p> on the reduced family. Its non-finiteness fields come from the ambient cokernel calculus: homogeneity of \(N' + x \cdot N\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_coker_isHomogeneous">1058</a>), the nesting \(N' + x \cdot N \le N\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_coker_le">1060</a>), and stability under the reduced family (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_coker_stable_full">1082</a>). The finiteness field is obtained by enlarging the denominator from \(N'\) to \(N' + x \cdot N\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyQuot_finite_of_le_denominator">1079</a>) to get \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r]\)-finiteness of the cokernel subquotient, then transferring down one variable (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_finite_transfer">1080</a>), valid because \(x\) annihilates the cokernel subquotient (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_coker_annihilate">1062</a>). This realises the cokernel half of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_ker_coker">1065</a> as a genuine length-\(r\) datum. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:5461:<p> on the reduced family \((t_0, \dots , t_{r-1})\). Its non-finiteness fields are supplied by the ambient kernel calculus: homogeneity of \(N \cap x^{-1}(N')\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_ker_isHomogeneous">1057</a>), the nesting \(N' \le N \cap x^{-1}(N')\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_ker_le">1059</a>), and stability under the reduced family (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_ker_stable_full">1081</a>). The finiteness witness is obtained by first shrinking the numerator from \(N\) to \(N \cap x^{-1}(N')\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyQuot_finite_of_le_numerator">1078</a>) to get \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r]\)-finiteness of the kernel subquotient, then transferring down one variable (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_finite_transfer">1080</a>), valid because \(x\) annihilates the kernel subquotient (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_ker_annihilate">1061</a>). This realises the kernel half of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_ker_coker">1065</a> as a genuine length-\(r\) datum. </p>

A \(\mathrm{GradedHilbert}\) datum for \((\kappa , f)\) is a natural number \(r\), an \(\mathbb {N}\)-graded \(\kappa \)-vector space \(M = \bigoplus _n M_n\) (an internal grading \(\mathcal{M} : \mathbb {N} \to \mathrm{Submodule}_\kappa M\) with \(\mathrm{DirectSum.Decomposition}\)) whose graded pieces \(M_n\) are all finite-dimensional, together with \(r\) pairwise-commuting \(\kappa \)-linear endomorphisms \(g_0, \dots , g_{r-1}\) that each raise the grading degree by one, such that \(\dim _\kappa M_n = f(n)\) for all \(n\) and \(M\) is a finite module over the polynomial ring \(\kappa [X_0, \dots , X_{r-1}]\) acting through the \(g_i\). This bundles exactly the data and hypotheses consumed by the graded Hilbert–Serre rationality engine <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:gradedHilbertSerre_rational">1016</a>. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:5766:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Existence of the Picard scheme]    The predicate \(\mathrm{HasPicScheme}(C)\) asserts that there exists a \(k\)-scheme \(X\), <em>locally of finite type over \(k\)</em>, carrying a representability witness for the relative Picard functor \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:pic_sharp_carrier">1538</a>; in other words, that the Picard scheme \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) exists and is locally of finite type. It is the existence assertion from which <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:pic_scheme">1536</a> extracts the representing object. The local-finiteness clause belongs to the same existence package as representability: Kleiman §4, Thm. th:main exhibits \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) as a disjoint union of open quasi-projective \(k\)-subschemes. The witness <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:inst_has_pic_scheme">1546</a> is conditional on the \(k\)-rational point of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:has_rational_point">1537</a>. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:5800:<p> is proper (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isProper_mathlib">1123</a>). Since properness is stable under base change (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isProper_mathlib">1123</a>), this condition is preserved by pull-back along any \(S'\to S\), which is exactly what the well-definedness of the Quot functor’s pullback action requires. </p>
