MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:5830:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[\(k\)-rational point]   The predicate \(\mathrm{HasRationalPoint}(C)\) asserts that the structural morphism \(C \to \operatorname{Spec}k\) admits a section \(\sigma : \operatorname{Spec}k \to C\), i.e. that \(C\) has a \(k\)-rational point. This is the standing hypothesis of the chapter (see <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#sec:fga_pic_setup">25.1</a>): by Kleiman §2, Thm. 2.5, it makes the plain relative Picard functor \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) coincide with its étale (and fppf) sheafification, so representability can be stated against <a href="chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html#def:rel_pic_sharp">621</a> directly. For a pointed curve \((C,P)\), the pointing \(P\) supplies this section. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:5860:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Representability of the smooth-proper quotient]   For a morphism \(\alpha : Z \to P\) of presheaves of types on \((\operatorname{Sch}/k)^{op}\), the predicate \(\mathrm{HasSmoothProperQuotient}(\alpha )\) asserts that the target \(P\) is representable. It records the conclusion of the Altman–Kleiman lemma <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#lem:smooth_proper_quotient">1534</a> for the quotient occurring in the FGA construction. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:5958:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Hilbert polynomial]    nitsure-hilbert-quot <i class="itshape">Source: [Nitsure], §1 (FGA Explained Ch. 5); cf. [Hartshorne], III.5.2.</i> Let \(X \to S\) be a finite-type morphism of noetherian schemes and let \(L\) be a line bundle on \(X\). For a coherent sheaf \(\mathcal{F}\) on \(X\) whose schematic support is proper over \(S\) and a point \(s \in S\), write \(X_s\) for the fibre over \(s\), \(\mathcal{F}_s = \mathcal{F}|_{X_s}\) and \(L_s = L|_{X_s}\). The <em>Hilbert polynomial of \(\mathcal{F}\) at \(s\) relative to \(L\)</em> is the unique polynomial \(\Phi _{\mathcal{F},s} \in \mathbb {Q}[\lambda ]\) that agrees, for all \(m \gg 0\), with the graded Hilbert function (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:fiber_hilbert_function">1011</a>) </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:5962:<p> of the section module \(\bigoplus _{m \ge 0} \Gamma (X_s, \mathcal{F}_s \otimes L_s^{\otimes m})\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:sectionGradedModule">1010</a>), viewed as a finitely generated graded module over the homogeneous section ring \(\bigoplus _{m \ge 0} \Gamma (X_s, L_s^{\otimes m})\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:sectionGradedRing">1009</a>). Uniqueness of \(\Phi _{\mathcal{F},s}\) is unconditional (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:hilbertPolynomial_unique">1026</a>: two polynomials agreeing at all sufficiently large integers coincide); existence, for \(X_s\) proper over \(\kappa (s)\), \(L_s\) ample and \(\mathcal{F}_s\) coherent, is the content of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#thm:hilbertPoly_of_sectionModule">1031</a>. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:6027:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Identity component of a group scheme]    <i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §5, Lem. 5.1.</i> Let \(k\) be a field and \(G\) a \(k\)-group scheme locally of finite type whose identity section \(e : \operatorname{Spec}k \to G\) factors through \(G\). The <em>identity component</em> of \(G\), denoted \(G^0\), is the locally closed subscheme of \(G\) whose underlying topological space is the connected component of \(|G|\) containing the image of \(e\), equipped with the reduced-induced (a priori) subscheme structure inherited from \(G\). In characteristic zero, or more generally when \(G\) has a geometrically reduced open subscheme, the substructure agrees with the open subscheme structure of <a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#thm:identity_component_open_subgroup">1552</a>. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:6245:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Local-finiteness assertion]    Whenever <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:has_pic_scheme">1545</a> holds, the second component of its chosen witness gives local finiteness of \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\). Thus representability and local finiteness are supplied by one existence package, as in Kleiman §4, Thm. th:main. </p>

Thus the type of line bundles on the product is </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:7068:<p><em>Well-definedness on basic opens.</em> The coherence condition for an ideal sheaf requires that, for an affine open \(U\) and \(f \in \mathcal{O}_X(U)\), the section \(\mathrm{Ann}(\mathcal{F})(U)\) restricts correctly to the basic open \(D(f) \subseteq U\), i.e. that \(\mathrm{Ann}_{\mathcal{O}_X(D(f))}(\mathcal{F}(D(f)))\) is the extension of \(\mathrm{Ann}_{\mathcal{O}_X(U)}(\mathcal{F}(U))\) along the localization map \(\mathcal{O}_X(U) \to \mathcal{O}_X(D(f))\). This is exactly where the two hypotheses enter. The bridge <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen">1247</a> supplies, for a quasi-coherent finite-type \(\mathcal{F}\), that \(\mathcal{O}_X(D(f)) = (\mathcal{O}_X(U))_f\) and that the restriction \(\mathcal{F}(U) \to \mathcal{F}(D(f))\) exhibits \(\mathcal{F}(D(f))\) as the localized module \((\mathrm{powers}\, f)^{-1} \mathcal{F}(U)\); the algebra engine <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:annihilator_localization_eq_map">1094</a> then yields, using that \(\mathcal{F}(U)\) is finitely generated, the required identity \(\mathrm{Ann}_{(\mathcal{O}_X(U))_f}\bigl((\mathrm{powers}\, f)^{-1} \mathcal{F}(U)\bigr) = \mathrm{Ann}_{\mathcal{O}_X(U)}(\mathcal{F}(U)) \cdot (\mathcal{O}_X(U))_f\). Thus the local annihilators are compatible with basic-open restriction, which is the patching datum that makes \(\mathrm{Ann}(\mathcal{F})\) a well-defined ideal sheaf. The finite-type hypothesis is genuinely required: without finite generation of \(\mathcal{F}(U)\) the annihilator need not commute with localization, and the local data fail to patch. </p>

The <em>Picard scheme</em> \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) is the \(k\)-scheme representing the relative Picard functor \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) (equivalently, by Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 under the rational point, its étale sheafification), supplied by <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#thm:fga_pic_representability">1533</a>, equipped with the abelian-group-scheme structure of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#thm:pic_is_group_scheme">1535</a>. MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:7873:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §5, opening + Prp. 5.3.</i> Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field \(k\). The <em>identity component of the Picard scheme</em> \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) is the identity component \((\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k})^0\) of the \(k\)-group scheme \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:pic_scheme">1536</a>, in the sense of <a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#def:identity_component_group_scheme">1551</a>. MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29045:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Homogeneity of the cokernel pair’s upper module]    Under the same hypotheses, the cokernel pair’s upper module \(N' + x \cdot N\) is homogeneous: it is the sum (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_sup_isHomogeneous">1054</a>) of the homogeneous \(N'\) with the homogeneous image \(x \cdot N\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_map_isHomogeneous">1052</a>). </p>

Hence the cokernel pair \((N,\,  N' + x \cdot N)\) is a valid subquotient pair (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientHilb">1046</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29105:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[The cokernel pair’s upper module is stable under the full family]    Under the same hypotheses, the cokernel pair’s upper module \(N' + x \cdot N\) is stable under every \(t_i\) (\(0 \le i \le r\)): each \(t_i\) preserves \(N'\) and preserves the image \(x \cdot N\) because it commutes with \(x\) and preserves \(N\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_map_map_le_of_commute">1064</a>), and a map preserves a sum of preserved submodules. This full stability supports the over-\(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r]\) finiteness input of the cokernel constructor. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29297:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Base-case finiteness over the empty polynomial ring]   Let \(Q\) be a \(\kappa \)-vector space that is also a module over \(\operatorname {MvPolynomial}(\sigma , \kappa )\) for an <em>empty</em> index set \(\sigma \) – in particular \(\sigma = \{ 0, \dots , r-1\} \) with \(r = 0\) – in a way compatible with the \(\kappa \)-action (scalar tower). If \(Q\) is module-finite over \(\operatorname {MvPolynomial}(\sigma , \kappa )\), then \(Q\) is finite-dimensional over \(\kappa \). Indeed for empty \(\sigma \) the polynomial ring is \(\operatorname {MvPolynomial}(\sigma , \kappa ) \cong \kappa \), a finite \(\kappa \)-module, so finiteness of \(Q\) over it transfers to finiteness over \(\kappa \) along the scalar tower. This is the length-zero input to the ambient subquotient induction (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_isRatHilb">1089</a>): when \(r = 0\) the subquotient \(N/N'\) is a finite-dimensional \(\kappa \)-vector space, hence \(\mathrm{hilb}\) is eventually zero. </p>

Project-local helper consumed by the two kernel-dimension computations of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_degreewise_diff">1067</a>. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29515:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Homogeneity of the kernel pair’s lower module]    Let \(x\) raise degree by one (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_raisesDegree">1047</a>) and let \(N, N'\) be homogeneous submodules of \(M\). Then the kernel pair’s lower module \(N \cap x^{-1}(N')\) is homogeneous. Indeed it is the intersection (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_inf_isHomogeneous">1053</a>) of the homogeneous \(N\) with the homogeneous preimage \(x^{-1}(N')\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_comap_isHomogeneous">1051</a>). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29518:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_ker_isHomogeneous">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29545:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[The kernel pair nests]   If \(N' \le N\) and \(x\) preserves \(N'\) (\(x \cdot N' \subseteq N'\)), then \(N' \le N \cap x^{-1}(N')\). Indeed \(N' \le N\) by hypothesis, and \(x \cdot N' \subseteq N'\) is exactly \(N' \subseteq x^{-1}(N')\); so \(N'\) is below the intersection. Hence the kernel pair \((N \cap x^{-1}(N'),\,  N')\) is a valid subquotient pair (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientHilb">1046</a>). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29548:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_ker_le">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29575:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[The kernel pair’s lower module is stable under the full family]    Let \((N, N')\) be a length-\((r+1)\) subquotient datum (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientHilb">1046</a>) with endomorphisms \(t_0, \dots , t_r\) and \(x = t_r\). Then the kernel pair’s lower module \(N \cap x^{-1}(N')\) is stable under <em>every</em> \(t_i\) (\(0 \le i \le r\)), not only the reduced family: each \(t_i\) preserves \(N\) and preserves the preimage \(x^{-1}(N')\) because it commutes with \(x\) and preserves \(N'\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_comap_map_le_of_commute">1063</a>). This full stability is what allows the kernel subquotient’s finiteness to be measured over \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r]\) before the transfer drops the last variable. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29578:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_ker_stable_full">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29609:<p> obtained by evaluation: it sends the last variable \(X_r\) to \(0\) and each earlier variable \(X_i\) (for \(0 \le i {\lt} r\)) to \(X_i\), and fixes constants. It is a left inverse of the algebra map \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}] \to \kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r]\) induced by the canonical inclusion \(\{ 0, \dots , r-1\}  \hookrightarrow \{ 0, \dots , r\} \) on variable indices, and is therefore surjective. This is the concrete ring surjection \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r] \twoheadrightarrow \kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\) along which finiteness is transferred (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:fg_restrictScalars_of_surjective_mathlib">1035</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29732:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Evaluation sends a constant to a scalar]    \(\mathrm{polyEndHom}(t)(C\, c) = c \cdot \mathrm{id}_M\) for each \(c \in \kappa \): the evaluation homomorphism (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyEndHom">1068</a>) is \(\kappa \)-linear and carries the constant polynomial \(C\, c\) to the scalar endomorphism \(c \cdot 1\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29766:<p> In words: acting by \(s\) through the full family \(t\) agrees, modulo \(P'\), with first projecting away the last variable via \(\mathrm{lastVarAlgHom}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_lastVarAlgHom">1075</a>) and acting through the reduced family \((t_0, \dots , t_{r-1})\). This is the semilinearity identity that makes the \(\sigma \)-semilinear quotient map of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_finite_transfer">1080</a> well-defined. The proof is induction on \(s\): the case of an earlier variable \(s = X_i\) (\(i {\lt} r\)) is the inductive hypothesis after \(\mathrm{lastVarAlgHom}\) fixes it; the case of the last variable \(s = X_r\) annihilates the reduced term, and the full term lands in \(P'\) because \(x = t_r\) carries \(P\) into the \(t\)-stable \(P'\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyEndHom_mem_of_stable">1076</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29796:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[A \(t\)-stable submodule is closed under the polynomial action]    Let \(t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}\) be pairwise-commuting \(\kappa \)-linear endomorphisms of \(M\) and let \(P' \subseteq M\) be a \(\kappa \)-submodule stable under each \(t_i\) (\(t_i \cdot P' \subseteq P'\)). Then \(P'\) is closed under the action of every polynomial: for all \(p \in \kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\) and \(m \in P'\), \(\mathrm{polyEndHom}(t)(p)(m) \in P'\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyEndHom">1068</a>). The proof is induction on \(p\): a constant acts as a scalar (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyEndHom_C">1070</a>), multiplication by a variable acts as the stabilising \(t_i\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyEndHom_X">1069</a>), and sums are handled additively. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29799:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyEndHom_mem_of_stable">LaTeX</a>

Immediate from the construction (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyEndHom">1068</a>), as evaluation sends \(X_i\) to the chosen image \(t_i\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29829:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyEndHom_X">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29856:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[A constant acts as a scalar]    In the polynomial-module structure (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyModule">1071</a>), \((C\, c) \cdot m = c \cdot m\) for all \(c \in \kappa \), \(m \in M\). Immediate from \(\mathrm{polyEndHom}(t)(C\, c) = c \cdot \mathrm{id}_M\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyEndHom_C">1070</a>). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29859:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyModule_C_smul">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29886:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[\(X_i\) acts as \(t_i\)]    In the polynomial-module structure (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyModule">1071</a>), \(X_i \cdot m = t_i(m)\) for all \(m \in M\). Immediate from \(\mathrm{polyEndHom}(t)(X_i) = t_i\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyEndHom_X">1069</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29916:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Enlarging the denominator preserves finiteness]    Let \(N\) and \(P_1 \le P_2\) be \(\kappa \)-submodules of \(M\), each stable under the commuting family \(t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}\), and suppose the subquotient \(N/P_1\) is finite over \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyModule">1071</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polySubmodule">1074</a>). Then \(N/P_2\) is also finite over \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\). Indeed the inclusion \(P_1 \subseteq P_2\) gives a surjection \(N/P_1 \twoheadrightarrow N/P_2\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:submodule_liftQ_mathlib">1040</a>), and finiteness transfers along it (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:module_finite_of_surjective_mathlib">1038</a>). This supplies the finiteness witness of the cokernel constructor (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientDatum_coker">1084</a>). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29919:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyQuot_finite_of_le_denominator">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:29946:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Shrinking the numerator preserves finiteness]    Let \(N_1 \le N_2\) and \(P'\) be \(\kappa \)-submodules of \(M\), each stable under the commuting family \(t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}\), and suppose the subquotient \(N_2/P'\) is finite over \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyModule">1071</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polySubmodule">1074</a>). Then \(N_1/P'\) is also finite over \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\). Indeed the inclusion \(N_1 \subseteq N_2\) induces an injective \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\)-linear map \(N_1/P' \hookrightarrow N_2/P'\); since \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\) is Noetherian (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:mvPolynomial_isNoetherianRing_fin_mathlib">1042</a>), the finite module \(N_2/P'\) is Noetherian (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isNoetherian_of_isNoetherianRing_of_finite_mathlib">1043</a>), so its submodule \(N_1/P'\) is finite (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:module_finite_of_injective_mathlib">1039</a>). This supplies the finiteness witness of the kernel constructor (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientDatum_ker">1083</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:30006:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Base case: the length-zero subquotient Hilbert function vanishes eventually]    <i class="itshape">Source: [Stacks Project], Tag 00K1 (base case of the induction).</i> Let \((N, N')\) be a subquotient datum of length \(0\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientHilb">1046</a>): a homogeneous pair \(N' \le N\) of the fixed ambient graded module \(M = \bigoplus _n \mathcal{M}_n\) with <em>no</em> endomorphisms, whose finiteness witness says the subquotient \(Q_0 := N/N'\) is module-finite over \(\operatorname {MvPolynomial}(\varnothing , \kappa )\). Then the ambient Hilbert function vanishes eventually: there is \(K \in \mathbb {N}\) with \(\mathrm{hilb}(n) = 0\) for all \(n {\gt} K\). Consequently \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(\mathrm{hilb}, 0)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:ratHilb_ofEventuallyZero">1020</a>), which is the base case of the ambient subquotient induction (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_isRatHilb">1089</a>). </p>

Let \(h_K\) and \(h_C\) be the Hilbert functions of the kernel and cokernel subquotients \(K = (N \cap x^{-1}(N'),\,  N')\) and \(C = (N,\,  N' + x \cdot N)\) of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_ker_coker">1065</a>. Then for every \(n\) </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:30040:<p> Writing \(Q_n = (N \cap \mathcal{M}_n)/(N' \cap \mathcal{M}_n)\) for the degree-\(n\) piece of \(N/N'\) (so \(\dim _\kappa Q_n = h_M(n)\)), multiplication by \(x\) is a \(\kappa \)-linear map \(x : Q_n \to Q_{n+1}\) with \(\ker (x : Q_n \to Q_{n+1})\) the degree-\(n\) piece of \(K\) and \(Q_{n+1}/\operatorname {im} x\) the degree-\((n+1)\) piece of \(C\); the identity is then the degreewise rank–nullity difference \(D_5\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_degreewise_finrank_diff">1085</a>). Specialising to \((N, N') = (\top , \bot )\) recovers the classical \(0 \to \mathcal{M}_n \xrightarrow {x} \mathcal{M}_{n+1} \to \mathcal{M}_{n+1}/x\mathcal{M}_n \to 0\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:30070:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Abstract single-pair finiteness transfer down one variable]    Let \(t_0, \dots , t_r\) be pairwise-commuting \(\kappa \)-linear endomorphisms of \(M\), and let \(P' \le P\) be \(\kappa \)-submodules of \(M\), each stable under every \(t_i\). Suppose the last endomorphism \(x = t_r\) carries \(P\) into \(P'\) (\(x \cdot P \subseteq P'\)), and that the subquotient \(P/P'\) is finite over the free polynomial ring \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r]\) for the polynomial-module structure of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyModule">1071</a> (with carriers the ambient \(t\)-stable submodules \(\mathrm{polySubmodule}\, P\), \(\mathrm{polySubmodule}\, P'\), <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polySubmodule">1074</a>). Then \(P/P'\) is finite over \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\) for the reduced family \((t_0, \dots , t_{r-1})\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:30071:<p>This is the abstract single-pair transfer: it does not mention the kernel/cokernel pairs, but is the engine applied to each of them by the kernel and cokernel constructors (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientDatum_ker">1083</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientDatum_coker">1084</a>). Because the last variable annihilates the subquotient, the \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r]\)-action factors through the last-variable surjection \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_r] \twoheadrightarrow \kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\), which is what makes the transfer drop one variable. </p>

Then \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(\mathrm{hilb}, r)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:ratHilb">1019</a>): the difference \(n \mapsto \dim _\kappa (N \cap \mathcal{M}_n) - \dim _\kappa (N' \cap \mathcal{M}_n)\) is, for \(n \gg 0\), the coefficient sequence of a rational series \(p \cdot (1 - X)^{-r}\) with \(p \in \mathbb {Q}[X]\). The induction is on the length \(r\), and every object that appears is an ambient pair of homogeneous submodules of the fixed graded module \(M\). </p>

Then the graded Hilbert function \(m \mapsto \dim _{\kappa (s)} \Gamma (X_s, F_s \otimes L_s^{\otimes m})\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:hilbert_polynomial">1006</a>) admits a \(\mathrm{GradedHilbert}\) datum over the residue field \(\kappa (s)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:gradedHilbert">1212</a>). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:30238:<p><em>Status.</em> This is <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:sectionGradedModule_fg">1012</a> (Serre) restated in engine-ready form; its Lean statement is a named leaf. Taking \(M\) to be the fibre section module \(M(X_s, F_s, L_s)\) and the \(d+1\) generators to be the homogeneous coordinate sections of the very ample embedding \(X_s \hookrightarrow \mathbb {P}^d_{\kappa (s)}\), the content is the finite generation of \(M(X_s, F_s, L_s)\) over the homogeneous coordinate ring \(\kappa (s)[x_0, \dots , x_d]\) — the finiteness of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:sectionGradedModule_fg">1012</a> together with the degree-one coordinate action. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:30268:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>    If \((\kappa , f)\) admits a \(\mathrm{GradedHilbert}\) datum of order \(r\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:gradedHilbert">1212</a>), then \(f\) is a rational Hilbert function of order \(r\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:ratHilb">1019</a>): there are \(p \in \mathbb {Q}[X]\) and \(N\) with \(f(n) = [X^n]\bigl(p \cdot (1-X)^{-r}\bigr)\) for all \(n {\gt} N\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:30302:<p> that is, the Hilbert series \(\sum _{n \ge 0} (\dim _\kappa M_n)\,  X^n\) is, up to a polynomial correction in low degrees, the rational function \(p \cdot (1 - X)^{-d}\), expressed in the power-series form \(\operatorname {toPowerSeries}(p) \cdot \operatorname {invOneSubPow}(\mathbb {Q}, d)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:invOneSubPow_mathlib">1015</a>). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:30303:<p><em>Status.</em> This is the substantive half of the graded Hilbert–Serre theorem (rationality of the Hilbert series of a finitely generated graded module). It is not covered by Mathlib: <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:hilbertPoly_exists_mathlib">1013</a> supplies only the converse polynomial-extraction step from a rational series, not the production of the rational series from the module. The argument is realised by an <em>ambient subquotient induction</em> (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_isRatHilb">1089</a>): the whole induction ranges over pairs of homogeneous submodules \(N' \le N\) of the single fixed graded module \(M\), and the Hilbert function is the ambient difference \(n \mapsto \dim _\kappa (N \cap M_n) - \dim _\kappa (N' \cap M_n)\). The class of such pairs is closed under the kernel and cokernel of multiplication by a degree-one element (each presented again as an ambient subquotient pair), so the inductive step never forms a graded quotient ring \(R/(x)\), a graded quotient module \(M/xM\), or a regrading of a derived carrier. The genuine Mathlib gap is thereby <em>avoided</em> rather than filled; the residual obligation is the short ambient bookkeeping of the subquotient blocks (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_subquotientHilb">1046</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_ker_coker">1065</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_degreewise_diff">1067</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_finite_transfer">1080</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_isRatHilb">1089</a>), each of which manipulates only ambient families \(n \mapsto N_{\mathrm{aux}} \cap M_n\) of submodules of \(M\). </p>

Then for all \(m \gg 0\) the Hilbert polynomial of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:hilbert_polynomial">1006</a> satisfies </p>

If \(\Phi , \Psi \in \mathbb {Q}[\lambda ]\) both agree with \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) at all sufficiently large integers – there are \(N_1, N_2 \in \mathbb {N}\) with \(\Phi (m) = h_{\mathcal{F},s}(m)\) for all \(m {\gt} N_1\) and \(\Psi (m) = h_{\mathcal{F},s}(m)\) for all \(m {\gt} N_2\) – then \(\Phi = \Psi \). Then the ideal \(\mathrm{span}\, s\) is a homogeneous ideal. In particular, for \(x \in R_1\) the principal ideal \((x)\) is homogeneous, hence \(xM\) and the auxiliary submodule \(N' + x \cdot N\) are homogeneous; this homogeneity feeds the kernel/cokernel closure (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_ker_coker">1065</a>). </p>

If \(a \in R\) is homogeneous of degree \(i\) – in particular \(x \in R_1\) – then for \(m \in M_n\) one has \(a \cdot m \in M_{i+n}\). This is the degree-shifting property that makes \(xM\) a homogeneous submodule (with degree-\((n+1)\) part \(x \cdot M_n\)) and that underlies the ambient identity \(x \cdot N \cap M_{n+1} = x \cdot (N \cap M_n)\) used in the subquotient closure (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_ker_coker">1065</a>) and difference identity (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_subquotient_degreewise_diff">1067</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:32740:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>    Let \(M\) be a sheaf of modules on \(\operatorname{Spec}R\) equipped with quasi-coherence data: an open cover \(\{ X_i\} \) of \(\operatorname{Spec}R\) together with, for each \(i\), a presentation of the slice restriction \(M.\mathrm{over}\, X_i\) — an exhibition of it as the cokernel of a map between coproducts of copies of the unit module. Let \(r \in R\) with \(D(r) \subseteq X_i\) for some \(i\), and let \(W := \iota _{X_i}^{-1}(D(r))\) be the corresponding affine open of the subscheme \(Z := X_i\). Then the restriction of \(M\) to \(D(r)\) — the pullback of \(M\) to \(Z\), then to \(W\), transported across the affine identification \(W \cong \operatorname{Spec}\Gamma (Z, W)\) — has invertible tilde–\(\Gamma \) counit (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib">1244</a>); that is, \(M|_{D(r)}\) is the tilde of its section module over \(\Gamma (Z, W) \cong R_r\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isLocalization_basicOpen_mathlib">1093</a>). </p>

[Nitsure], “Construction of Hilbert and Quot Schemes”, §1, where \(\operatorname {Hilb}_{X/S} = \operatorname {Quot}_{\mathcal{O}_X/X/S}\)).</i> Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve. There is a natural transformation of presheaves on \((\operatorname{Sch}/k)^{op}\) </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:35083:<p> (\(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) the relative-divisor functor of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:div_functor_carrier">1540</a>, \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) the relative Picard functor of <a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:pic_sharp_carrier">1538</a>), with the following <em>defining property</em>: at a \(T\)-point represented by a family \(\langle \mathcal F, q\rangle \) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:div_family">1147</a>: a finitely presented, \(T\)-flat quotient \(q \colon \mathcal O_{C\times _kT}\twoheadrightarrow \mathcal F\) whose kernel is an invertible ideal sheaf cutting out a relative effective divisor \(D\subseteq C\times _kT\)), </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:35087:<p> the class of the associated invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_{C \times _k T}(D)\), i.e. the additive inverse of the class of the ideal sheaf \(\ker q\) (Kleiman §3, Def. dfn:Abel). This transformation is the required witness for \(\mathrm{HasAbelMap}(C)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:has_abel_map">1542</a>). </p>

Then the section over \(U\) of the annihilator ideal sheaf \(\mathrm{Ann}(\mathcal{F})\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:modules_annihilator">1090</a>) is contained in the module-annihilator of the sections of \(\mathcal{F}\) over \(U\): </p>

Proved directly in Lean. It supports the well-definedness of the schematic support (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:schematic_support">1121</a>). </p>

Then the multivariate polynomial ring \(\operatorname {MvPolynomial}(\{ 0, \dots , r-1\} , R)\) is a Noetherian ring (Hilbert’s basis theorem in finitely many variables). With \(R = \kappa \) a field this makes \(\kappa [t_0, \dots , t_{r-1}]\) Noetherian, the base ring over which the subquotient finiteness is measured (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:graded_polyQuot_finite_of_le_numerator">1078</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:38829:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[The Grothendieck-slice restriction equals the geometric restriction (gap1, C)]    <i class="itshape">The one lemma that must touch the Grothendieck slice site; everything downstream of it is geometric.</i> Let \(X\) be a scheme and \(U \subseteq X\) an open. The <em>abstract Grothendieck-slice</em> restriction \(M.\mathrm{over}\, U\) — an object of the category of sheaves of modules over the sliced structure sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_X.\mathrm{over}\, U\) on the slice site \(J.\mathrm{over}\, U\) — is canonically isomorphic to the <em>geometric</em> restriction \((\mathrm{restrictFunctor}\, U.\iota ).\mathrm{obj}\, M\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_restrictFunctor_mathlib">1098</a>), equivalently to the pullback \(U.\iota ^{*} M\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_mathlib">1099</a>), as a sheaf of modules on the small Zariski site of the open subscheme \(U.\mathrm{toScheme}\). The isomorphism is induced by the equivalence of sites \(J.\mathrm{over}\, U \simeq \mathrm{Opens}(U.\mathrm{toScheme})\) coming from the opens functor of the open immersion \(U.\iota \), under which the sliced sheaf of rings \(\mathcal{O}_X.\mathrm{over}\, U\) corresponds to the structure sheaf of \(U.\mathrm{toScheme}\). For \(X = \operatorname{Spec}R\) and \(U = D(r)\) a basic open, the target category is \((\operatorname{Spec}R_r).\mathrm{Modules}\) under the affine identification \(D(r) \cong \operatorname{Spec}R_r\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isLocalization_basicOpen_mathlib">1093</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:38859:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[The slice-to-geometric isomorphism in pullback form (gap1, C, step 4’)]    <i class="itshape">The pullback packaging of the slice-touching bridge; the form consumed by the P1 transport.</i> With \(X\) and \(U \subseteq X\) as above and \(M\) a sheaf of modules on \(X\), the transport of the abstract Grothendieck-slice restriction \(M.\mathrm{over}\, U\) under the step-3 equivalence functor (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:over_restrict_equiv">1108</a>) is canonically isomorphic to the inverse-image (pullback) of \(M\) along the open immersion \(U.\iota \): </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:38863:<p> (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:modules_pullback_mathlib">1097</a>). This is the pullback packaging of the slice-touching bridge <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:over_restrict_iso">1109</a>; it is exactly the form in which a presentation of \(M.\mathrm{over}\, U\) is transported into a presentation of the geometric pullback \(U.\iota ^{*}M\), and it is the ingredient consumed by the per-element local-tilde transport <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:isIso_fromTildeΓ_basicOpen_of_quasicoherent">1111</a>. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:38866:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:over_restrict_pullback_iso">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:38967:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[The over-equivalence functor is cocontinuous]    <i class="itshape">Topological layer of bridge C; fills the <span class="ttfamily">Topology/Sheaves/Over.lean</span> TODO.</i> The functor of \(\mathrm{Opens.overEquivalence}\, U\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:opens_overEquivalence_mathlib">1100</a>) is cocontinuous (cover-lifting) from the \(U\)-slice \(J_X|_U\) of the opens Grothendieck topology of \(X\) to the opens Grothendieck topology \(J_U\) of the subspace \(U\). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:38970:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:overEquivalence_functor_isCocontinuous">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:38997:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[The over-equivalence functor is continuous]    <i class="itshape">Topological layer of bridge C; needed for the module-level lift of step 3.</i> The functor of \(\mathrm{Opens.overEquivalence}\, U\) is continuous (cover-preserving) for \((J_X|_U, J_U)\). It is obtained from the cocontinuity of the inverse (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:overEquivalence_inverse_isCocontinuous">1103</a>) through the equivalence adjunction: the left adjoint of a cocontinuous functor is continuous. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:39000:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:overEquivalence_functor_isContinuous">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:39030:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:overEquivalence_inverse_isCocontinuous">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:39057:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[The over-equivalence inverse is continuous]    <i class="itshape">Topological layer of bridge C; needed for the module-level lift of step 3.</i> Symmetrically, the inverse of \(\mathrm{Opens.overEquivalence}\, U\) is continuous for \((J_U, J_X|_U)\), obtained from the cocontinuity of the functor (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:overEquivalence_functor_isCocontinuous">1102</a>) through the equivalence adjunction. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:39060:    <a class="latex_link" href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:overEquivalence_inverse_isContinuous">LaTeX</a>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:39087:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[The over-equivalence inverse is a dense subsite]    <i class="itshape">Topological layer of bridge C; the dense-subsite witness assembled from the two cocontinuities.</i> The inverse of \(\mathrm{Opens.overEquivalence}\, U\) is a dense subsite for \((J_U, J_X|_U)\). This is formal: an equivalence both of whose legs are cocontinuous (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:overEquivalence_functor_isCocontinuous">1102</a>, <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:overEquivalence_inverse_isCocontinuous">1103</a>) yields a dense subsite on its inverse. </p>

If \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(g, e)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:ratHilb">1019</a>) and \(g\) is the first difference of \(H\) beyond \(N\) (\(H(n+1) - H(n) = g(n+1)\) for all \(n {\gt} N\)), then \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(H, e+1)\). This is the predicate-level packaging of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:rationalHilbert_antidiff">1018</a>: a finite difference raises the pole order by one, the inductive heart of graded Hilbert–Serre. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:45744:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Raising the pole order]    If \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(f, d)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:ratHilb">1019</a>) then \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(f, d+1)\): multiplying the numerator by \((1-X)\) cancels one factor of \((1-X)^{-1}\), so the same coefficient sequence is realised at pole order \(d+1\). This lets two rational Hilbert functions of different orders be brought to a common denominator. Proved directly in Lean using \((1-X)\cdot (1-X)^{-(d+1)} = (1-X)^{-d}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:invOneSubPow_mathlib">1015</a>). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:45808:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Base case: eventually-zero functions are rational of order \(0\)]    If \(f : \mathbb {N} \to \mathbb {Q}\) is eventually zero – there is \(N\) with \(f(n) = 0\) for all \(n {\gt} N\) – then \(\mathrm{IsRatHilb}(f, 0)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:ratHilb">1019</a>). Indeed \(f\) is then the coefficient sequence of the numerator polynomial \(0\) over \((1-X)^{0} = 1\). This is the base case of the Stacks 00K1 induction (no degree-one generators). Proved directly in Lean. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:50529:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[The away-fraction bridge]    Through the chart identification of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:chart_sections_away">1206</a>, the two descent legs restricting to the overlap \(D_+(X_i X_j)\) are the localisation-algebra maps \(\mathrm{Away}(X_i) \to \mathrm{Away}(X_i X_j)\) and \(\mathrm{Away}(X_j) \to \mathrm{Away}(X_i X_j)\) sending a fraction to its image under the further localisation at the other variable, followed by the canonical identification of \(\mathrm{Away}(X_i X_j)\) with itself along the two orderings of the product. </p>

Through the \(i\)-chart trivialisation, the second (“\(b\)”) descent leg sends a \(j\)-chart section \(y \in \Gamma (U_j, \mathcal O)\) to its restriction along the overlap immersion \(t_{ij} \circ f_{ji} : V_{ij} \to U_j\), scaled by the inverse transition unit \((X_j/X_i)^m\): </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:50735:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[The degree-\(m\) forms embed as global sections of \(\mathcal O(m)\)]    There is an additive homomorphism from the degree-\(m\) homogeneous forms of \(\mathbb Z[X_i : i \in n]\) to \(\Gamma \bigl(\operatorname {Proj} \mathbb Z[X_i], \mathcal O(m)\bigr)\), sending \(F\) to the global section corresponding, under <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:serre_twist_sections_compatible">1203</a>, to the compatible chart family of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:serre_twist_form_compatible">1208</a>. When the index set \(n\) is nonempty, this homomorphism is injective: a global section is determined by any one of its chart fractions, and the \(i\)-chart fraction of the image of \(F\) recovers \(F\) since \(X_i\) is a nonzerodivisor of the domain \(\mathbb Z[X_i]\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:50804:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[Global sections of \(\mathcal O(m)\) are the degree-\(m\) forms]    For \(n\) nonempty, the embedding of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#lem:serre_twist_forms_embed">1209</a> of the degree-\(m\) homogeneous forms of \(\mathbb Z[X_i : i \in n]\) into \(\Gamma \bigl(\operatorname {Proj}\mathbb Z[X_i], \mathcal O(m)\bigr)\) is onto: every global section of \(\mathcal O(m)\) arises from a (unique) degree-\(m\) form, i.e. \(\Gamma \bigl(\operatorname {Proj}\mathbb Z[X_i], \mathcal O(m)\bigr) \cong (\mathbb Z[X_i])_m\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:50918:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[The Serre twist is a locally trivial line bundle]    For every \(m \ge 0\), the Serre twisting sheaf \(\mathcal{O}(m)\) on the integral model \(\operatorname {Proj} \mathbb {Z}[X_i : i \in n]\) and its base change \(\mathcal{O}(m)\) on \(\mathbb {P}(n; S)\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:twisting_sheaf">1181</a>) are locally trivial line bundles (<a href="chap-Picard_LineBundlePullback.html#def:IsLocallyTrivial">597</a>): rank-one free on each member of the standard affine cover \(\{ D_+(X_i)\} \). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:59138:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>[FGA representability of the Picard scheme]    <i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §4, Main Thm. 4.8 + Cor. 4.18.3.</i> Let \(k\) be a field and \(C\) a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over \(k\) <em>with a \(k\)-rational point</em> (<a href="chap-Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.html#def:has_rational_point">1537</a>). Then the relative Picard functor \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}\) of <a href="chap-Picard_RelPicFunctor.html#def:rel_pic_sharp">621</a> — which under the rational-point hypothesis coincides with its étale sheafification \(\operatorname{Pic}_{(C/k)\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\), by Kleiman §2, Thm. 2.5 — is representable by a \(k\)-scheme \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\), separated and locally of finite type over \(k\), which is a disjoint union of open quasi-projective \(k\)-subschemes, each an increasing union of open quasi-projective subschemes. The scheme \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) is called the <em>Picard scheme</em> of \(C/k\). </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:59502:    <div class="thm_thmcontent"><p>    hilbert-serre-algebra Let \(M = \bigoplus _n \mathcal{M}_n\) be an \(\mathbb {N}\)-graded \(\kappa \)-vector space and \(t \colon \mathrm{Fin}\, r \to \mathrm{End}_\kappa (M)\) a finite family of pairwise commuting endomorphisms, each raising degree by one (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_raisesDegree">1047</a>), making \(M\) a module over \(\kappa [X_1, \dots , X_r]\) with \(X_i\) acting as \(t_i\) (<a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:graded_polyModule">1071</a>). If \(M\) is finitely generated over this polynomial ring, then every graded piece \(\mathcal{M}_n\) is finite-dimensional over \(\kappa \). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:59533:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Nitsure], §1, "Construction of Grassmannian" (FGA Explained Ch. 5).</i> Let \(S\) be a noetherian scheme, \(V\) a locally free \(\mathcal{O}_S\)-module of rank \(r\), and \(1 \le d \le r\). The functor \(\mathrm{Grass}(V,d)\) of <a href="chap-Picard_QuotScheme.html#def:grassmannian_scheme">1164</a> is representable by a smooth projective \(S\)-scheme \(\mathrm{Gr}_S(V, d) \to S\) of relative dimension \(d(r-d)\), equipped with a tautological quotient \(\pi ^* V \twoheadrightarrow \mathcal{U}\) of rank \(d\). The determinant line bundle \(\det (\mathcal{U})\) is relatively very ample, and the associated linear system gives a closed embedding \(\mathrm{Gr}_S(V, d) \hookrightarrow \mathbb {P}_S\! \left(\bigwedge ^d V\right)\) – the <em>Plücker embedding</em>. </p>

MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:59784:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §5, Lem. 5.1 (3); the verbatim source quote of (3) is at <a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#thm:identity_component_open_subgroup">1552</a>.</i> Let \(k\) be a field, \(G\) a \(k\)-group scheme locally of finite type, and \(K/k\) a field extension. The natural map \((G^0)_K \to (G_K)^0\), induced by base-changing the inclusion of <a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#thm:identity_component_open_subgroup">1552</a> along \(\operatorname{Spec}K \to \operatorname{Spec}k\) and using the universal property of the identity component on \(G_K\), is an isomorphism of \(K\)-schemes. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:59815:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §5, Lem. 5.1 (3); the verbatim source quote of (3) is at <a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#thm:identity_component_open_subgroup">1552</a>.</i> Let \(k\) be a field and \(G\) a \(k\)-group scheme locally of finite type. Then the identity component \(G^0\) is of finite type over \(k\) — equivalently, locally of finite type <em>and</em> quasi-compact — and geometrically irreducible: after base change to the algebraic closure \(\bar k\), the underlying scheme \(G^0_{\bar k}\) is an irreducible \(\bar k\)-scheme. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:59846:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §5, Lem. 5.1 (3); the verbatim source quote of (3) is at <a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#thm:identity_component_open_subgroup">1552</a>.</i> Let \(k\) be a field and \(G\) a \(k\)-group scheme locally of finite type. The clopen inclusion \(G^0 \hookrightarrow G\) (<a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#thm:identity_component_open_subgroup">1552</a>) is a homomorphism of \(k\)-group schemes: \(G^0\) inherits a \(k\)-group-scheme structure from \(G\), and the inclusion morphism in the over-category over \(\operatorname{Spec}k\) is compatible with the group laws on source and target. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:59877:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §5, Lem. 5.1 (3).</i> Let \(k\) be a field and \(G\) a \(k\)-group scheme locally of finite type. Then the identity component \(G^0\) (<a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#def:identity_component_group_scheme">1551</a>) is an open and closed subscheme of \(G\): the inclusion \(G^0 \hookrightarrow G\) is both an open immersion and a closed immersion of schemes. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:60329:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §5, Prp. 5.3 (geometric irreducibility of the connected component of the identity).</i> Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field \(k\). The identity component \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#def:pic_zero_subscheme">1576</a>) is geometrically irreducible: after base change to the algebraic closure \(\bar k\), the scheme \((\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k})_{\bar k}\) is irreducible. </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:60390:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Milne], “Abelian Varieties” (course notes, 2008), §I.1, p. 8 (definition of abelian variety); [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §5, Rmk. 5.26 (the Jacobian \(J := \operatorname{Pic}^0_{X/S}\) of a smooth proper family of curves is a projective abelian \(S\)-scheme).</i> Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve of genus \(g\) over a field \(k\). The identity component \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#def:pic_zero_subscheme">1576</a>) is an <em>abelian variety over \(k\)</em> of dimension \(g\): the underlying \(k\)-scheme is smooth (<a href="chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html#thm:pic0_smooth">1620</a>), proper (<a href="chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html#thm:pic0_proper">1621</a>), and geometrically irreducible (<a href="chap-Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.html#thm:pic0_geom_irred">1622</a>), and it carries a \(k\)-group-scheme structure inherited from \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) via the inclusion \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k} \hookrightarrow \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#thm:identity_component_is_subgroup_homomorphism">1553</a>). In particular, \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) is automatically commutative (Milne §I.1, Cor. 1.4). </p>
MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/dep_graph_document.html:60421:<p><i class="itshape">Source: [Kleiman], “The Picard scheme”, §5, Thm. 5.4; cf. The identity component \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\) (<a href="chap-Picard_IdentityComponent.html#def:pic_zero_subscheme">1576</a>) is projective over \(k\), in particular proper: the structural morphism \((\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}) \to \operatorname{Spec}k\) is a projective morphism, hence satisfies the universal closedness and separatedness conditions of properness. </p>

Then \(\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) is canonically an abelian group scheme over \(k\): the tensor product \([\mathcal{L}] + [\mathcal{M}] := [\mathcal{L} \otimes \mathcal{M}]\) and inverse \(-[\mathcal{L}] := [\mathcal{L}^{-1}]\) on \(\operatorname{Pic}^\sharp _{C/k}(T)\) (well defined because both operations preserve isomorphism classes and descend through the subgroup \(H_T = \pi _T^*\operatorname{Pic}(T)\) of <a href="chap-Picard_LineBundlePullback.html#thm:relative_pic_quotient_well_defined">604</a>) are natural in \(T\), hence by Yoneda are represented by morphisms \(m : \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k} \times _k \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k} \to \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\), \(i : \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k} \to \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\), and \(e : \operatorname{Spec}k \to \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\) (the trivial line bundle class) satisfying the abelian-group axioms. /-! ## The campaign spellings (the DAT-D windows) and the §4.1 bundle -/

section Curve

open Scheme Grassmannian

variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
variable (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (g r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
variable (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(divisorSections k B ⊤))
variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))

/-- The structure morphism of `DivScheme g` is **quasi-compact** — the Wave-5 qc input
toward `AbelSourceData.isProper` (§4.2 consumer row). -/
instance quasiCompact_divSchemeOverHom :
    QuasiCompact (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂).hom :=
  quasiCompact_carveSchemeOverHom k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)

/-- **`DivScheme g` is a compact space**: a closed subscheme of the compact
Grassmannian pair (§4.1: qc is free, no image argument). -/
instance compactSpace_divScheme : CompactSpace (DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) :=
  compactSpace_carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)

/-- The structure morphism of `DivScheme g` is **locally of finite type** — the
DAT-glue lft certificate of the 01JJ chart family (§4.2 consumer row). -/
instance locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom :
    LocallyOfFiniteType (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂).hom :=
  locallyOfFiniteType_carveSchemeOverHom k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)

/-- The structure morphism of `DivScheme g` is **separated** — with
`quasiCompact_divSchemeOverHom` and `locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom`, the
`IsProper` constituents short of universal closedness (§4.1 boundary). -/
instance isSeparated_divSchemeOverHom :
    IsSeparated (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂).hom :=
  isSeparated_carveSchemeOverHom k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)

/-- **`DivScheme g` is separated** (absolutely). -/
instance isSeparated_divScheme : (DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂).IsSeparated :=
  isSeparated_carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)

/-- **The `divQProj` certificate shape** (worksheet §4.1, verbatim): `DivScheme g` is
quasi-projective **as consumed** — the closed immersion into the Grassmannian pair,
the pair's finite affine frame atlas / qc / lft / separatedness data, and the derived
qc / lft / separatedness of `DivScheme g` over `k`.

Honest boundary (§4.1, BINDING): projectivity (Plücker) is NOT part of this bundle;
consumers needing an ample bundle or universal closedness must negotiate a new brick. -/
structure DivQProjBundle : Prop where
  /-- `DivScheme g ⟶ grPair` is a closed immersion (§3.1, closed in the pair). -/
  isClosedImmersion_ι : IsClosedImmersion (divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)
  /-- The pair's frame atlas is finite. -/
  finite_atlasIndex : Finite (grPairCover k g r₁ g r₂).I₀
  /-- Each patch of the pair's frame atlas is affine. -/
  isAffine_atlas : ∀ ij : (grPairCover k g r₁ g r₂).I₀,
    IsAffine ((grPairCover k g r₁ g r₂).X ij)
  /-- The pair is quasi-compact over `k`. -/
  quasiCompact_pairStructMap : QuasiCompact (grPairStructMap k g r₁ g r₂)
  /-- The pair is locally of finite type over `k`. -/
  locallyOfFiniteType_pairStructMap : LocallyOfFiniteType (grPairStructMap k g r₁ g r₂)
  /-- The pair is separated over `k`. -/
  isSeparated_pairStructMap : IsSeparated (grPairStructMap k g r₁ g r₂)
  /-- `DivScheme g` is quasi-compact over `k` (Wave-5 row). -/
  quasiCompact_hom : QuasiCompact (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂).hom
  /-- `DivScheme g` is locally of finite type over `k` (DAT-glue row). -/
  locallyOfFiniteType_hom : LocallyOfFiniteType (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂).hom
  /-- `DivScheme g` is separated over `k`. -/
  isSeparated_hom : IsSeparated (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂).hom

/-- **`divQProj`** (worksheet §4.1): the quasi-projectivity bundle of `DivScheme g`,
assembled — the single citable certificate for DAT-G's quasi-projective charts
(§4.2 consumer row, with the §4.1 Plücker boundary note). -/
theorem divQProj : DivQProjBundle k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ where
  isClosedImmersion_ι := isClosedImmersion_divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂
  finite_atlasIndex := finite_grPairCover_index k g r₁ g r₂
  isAffine_atlas ij := isAffine_grPairCover_X k g r₁ g r₂ ij
  quasiCompact_pairStructMap := quasiCompact_grPairStructMap k g r₁ g r₂
  locallyOfFiniteType_pairStructMap := locallyOfFiniteType_grPairStructMap k g r₁ g r₂
  isSeparated_pairStructMap := isSeparated_grPairStructMap k g r₁ g r₂
  quasiCompact_hom := quasiCompact_divSchemeOverHom k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂
  locallyOfFiniteType_hom := locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂
  isSeparated_hom := isSeparated_divSchemeOverHom k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂

end Curve

"$HORIZON_GIT" add -- MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0AdmissibleAbelKernel.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" diff --cached --name-status
